question:
Why does nco_confpack -export fail with the message "Tool in menu but not found"? 

I tried to export OMNIbus configuration using nco_confpack command and I get the following message:

Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: Close

I've also tried using it with -list command and I get the same error.

Why is this happening?
reference: The error "Tool in menu but not found" occurs because the menu AlertsMenu contains a tool called Close that no longer exists. The nco_confpack command is trying to export the configuration which includes this tool but since it is not found, the export fails. To resolve this issue, the tool Close needs to be recreated and associated with the menu AlertsMenu before trying to run the nco_confpack command again for exporting the configuration successfully.
contexts: tool; menu; not found; confpack TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) Migrating to a new version of Omnibus, running nco_confpack: $OMNIHOME/bin/nco_confpack -list -server NCOMS -user ncadmin -file /tmp/nco_confpack.list Received this error: Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: CLEAR_LWY. SYMPTOM The command fails and the following error is received: Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: CLEAR_LWY. CAUSE The menu AlertsMenu has a tool in it called CLEAR_LWY, however the tool no longer exists. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM Recreate the tool and associate it with the menu and try to run the command again.

confpack; objectserver; omnibus; two TECHNOTE (FAQ) QUESTION What causes the error: "Duplicate menu path: MapPageOVMenu" when using nco_confpack to export or import object server data? CAUSE Due to having 2 menus with the same name in the tools menu. ANSWER The solution is to rename or delete away (if no not needed) one of the duplicate menus. The object server is able to allow for duplicate menu item names because it tracks them by a numeric identifier in the database tables. For nco_confpack to be able to export and then import , it can't rely upon those numeric identifiers, because they will be different from one host to another, so we have to use the name. The menus and menu items are tracked by constructing a menu tree, starting from the root. Then the complete path is then used as the key. This allows for the menu and menu items to be unique, based upon a name. This is where the duplicate menu path comes into the picture. Solution : Make sure the names are unique. For example, append them with a sequential number (ie: by appending a 1, 2, 3....).

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP? 

I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.
reference:
To configure Decision Center to look for the SSP on a different application server, you can follow these steps:

1. Ensure that the application server where the SSP is deployed is accessible from the Decision Center server.

2. In Decision Center, go to the Configuration settings for the Rule Execution Server (RES) endpoint.

3. Change the endpoint URL to point to the hostname and port of the application server where the SSP is deployed. For example, if the RES console is on port 8000 and the SSP is on port 9000 on the separate server, the endpoint URL should be something like http://ssp_hostname:9000/sspService.

4. Save the configuration changes and restart Decision Center to apply the new settings.

By updating the RES endpoint URL to point to the hostname and port of the server where the SSP is deployed, Decision Center will now look for the SSP service on the specified server instead of assuming it is on the same server as the RES console.
contexts: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." RESOLVING THE PROBLEM This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://<host>:<port>/testing' instead of 'http://<host>:<port>/res" in the RTS configuration. . When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help > Configure: Manage your project configuration > Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs integrated into different SSPs. I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. reference:

I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.
reference:
To configure Decision Center to look for the SSP on a different application server, you can follow these steps:

1. Ensure that the application server where the SSP is deployed is accessible from the Decision Center server.

2. In Decision Center, go to the Configuration settings for the Rule Execution Server (RES) endpoint.

3. Change the endpoint URL to point to the hostname and port of the application server where the SSP is deployed. For example, if the RES console is on port 8000 and the SSP is on port 9000 on the separate server, the endpoint URL should be something like http://ssp_hostname:9000/sspService.

4. Save the configuration changes and restart Decision Center to apply the new settings.

By updating the RES endpoint URL to point to the hostname and port of the server where the SSP is deployed, Decision Center will now look for the SSP service on the specified server instead of assuming it is on the same server as the RES console.

reference:

REPORTED COMPONENT NAME: WMQ SOL SPARC

ERROR DESCRIPTION:
There was an issue related to the change of system hostname causing WebSphere MQ to lose some fault tolerance in relation to semaphore ID clashes. This issue affected systems on which the hostname has changed since installing WebSphere MQ.

question: Why does my JVMSERVER remain in a "BEING DISABLED"  state? When I try to disable a JVMSERVER it becomes hung and remains in a "BEING DISABLED" state. This also occurs when I shut down the CICS region. The CICS region ultimately has to be cancelled.
reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue with the JVMSERVER remaining in a "BEING DISABLED" state could be due to the zFS files not being properly propagated to the target environments after applying preventative maintenance to CICS Transaction Server for z/OS. When the updated zFS files are not rolled out to the target environments, it can impact the functioning of the JVM Servers.

To resolve this issue, ensure that the updated zFS files are properly propagated to all target environments when maintenance is applied to CICS. This should allow the JVMSERVER to be disabled successfully without getting stuck in a "BEING DISABLED" state.

question: Is there a scripting feature in ITM? Is there a scripting feature in ITM?
reference:
Yes, there is a scripting feature in IBM Tivoli Monitoring (ITM). The context provided mentions the "Custom Scripting" feature in ITM, which allows users to execute custom scripts and reports the output data through special attribute groups.

Specifically, the context mentions the following:

- There are custom scripts that can be executed in ITM, and the data gathered from executing these scripts is reported using the KXX_Custom_Scripts_Runtime attribute groups (where XX stands for LZ, NT, or UX).
- However, the custom scripts implementation in ITM 6.30 FP5 used "pure event" tables, which meant situations could not receive "clearing" events and needed to be manually closed.
- To address this, new KXX_Custom_Scripts_Rtm_Smp "sampled" tables were added, which report the same custom script output data but in a way that allows situations to receive clearing events.

So in summary, yes, ITM does have a custom scripting feature that allows users to execute their own scripts and have the output data monitored and reported within the ITM environment.
contexts: - NT for Windows OS agent This is an overview of the scripting feature; details will be provided in the following sections. The OS agent loops, at a configurable interval, looking for script definition property files (*.properties) in a configurable directory path. The property files are parsed and OS Monitoring Agent spawns a new process named “fcp_daemon” if at least one valid script definition is found. This new daemon is responsible for scheduling the script executions and gathering all information regarding running scripts. 1. Log on to Passport Advantage.

3. Enter your IBM ID and password, and click Sign in.
4. Click Software download and media access.
5. Click Download finder, and then click View all my downloads.

10. Unpack all other parts into separate temporary directories for each part.
11. Follow the instructions in the Quick Start Guide to install the product.

SYMPTOM CIWEB Error: com.ibm.ecm.beans.viewer.DocServicesSessionBean$ICNStreamingDocServices. _loadDocument java.io.IOException: No such file or directory CAUSE ICN creates a subdirectory under UNIX: /tmp or Windows:\temp for temporary file storage. On some systems, automated housecleaning procedures at OS level delete the contents of /tmp and its subdirectories, resulting in the error. DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM On startup, ICN sets the variable ENGINE_TEMPDIR which defines a temporary directory, for example: '/tmp/ECMClient.IBMWebSphereApplicationServer80.navigator.tmpdir' . Verify the directory path and check whether the directory exists or has been deleted. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM There are two ways to resolve the problem: 1) Disable the automation which deletes the contents of /tmp. Some Linux systems for example use a 'tmpwatch' process which deletes files in /tmp. For tmpwatch, an 'EXCLUDE' job parameter can be defined, causing the process to skip the named subdirectory. 2) ICN uses the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) default temp file directory, which can be overridden at JVM level by adding the Java system property java.io.tmpdir. For example, specify "-Djava.io.tmpdir=/var/temp" in the application server startup configuration. Note that this setting is JVM-wide and will affect all applications

question: For HP-UX how to write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout? A customer asked why no gc logs generated even if they use the -Xverbosegc option. So How can I write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout for HP-UX?
reference:
To write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout for HP-UX, you would need to add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments:

-XX:+PrintGCDetails 
-XX:+PrintGCDateStamps 
-XX:+PrintHeapAtGC 
-Xverbosegc:file=/tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc 

Additionally, to enable log file rotation, you should include the following parameters:
-XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation
-XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10
-XX:GCLogFileSize=10M 

These settings will allow you to write verbose gc output to a log file other than native_stdout on HP-UX and generate gc logs as needed.

question: Why is OCR is putting multiple lines on one line? I am running an APT application, and multiple detail lines are getting put on a single line within my .TXT file.  Is there something I can do about this?
reference:
Based on the context provided, it seems that the issue of multiple lines being merged into a single line is related to the NormalizeCCO function in the IBM Datacap Taskmaster Capture application. 

The key points from the context are:

1. After running NormalizeCCO, words on separate lines are merged into a single line of text when using IBM Datacap Taskmaster Capture.
2. This happens when the text is not cleanly printed in lines, such as when the font varies or the text is vertically offset.
3. The NormalizeCCO function goes through the CCO file and cleans up the entries so they appear in regular lines. 
4. However, for some complex images, NormalizeCCO cannot determine where to separate the lines and ends up merging all words into a single line.

To resolve this issue, the context suggests adding an action prior to running NormalizeCCO. This action allows you to specify the percentage of a line that two words must be offset to be considered as separate lines. By adjusting this setting, you can prevent the unwanted merging of lines.

So, in your case with the APT application, you could try adding a similar action before running NormalizeCCO to see if it helps prevent the multiple detail lines from being merged into a single line in the .TXT file.

2. This happens when the text is not cleanly printed in lines, such as when the font varies or the text is vertically offset.
3. The NormalizeCCO function goes through the CCO file and cleans up the entries so they appear in regular lines. 
4. However, for some complex images, NormalizeCCO cannot determine where to separate the lines and ends up merging all words into a single line.

To resolve this issue, the context suggests adding an action prior to running NormalizeCCO. This action allows you to specify the percentage of a line that two words must be offset to be considered as separate lines. By adjusting this setting, you can prevent the unwanted merging of lines.

question: StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases There is much published documentation about stale connections to databases on the web, and yet stale connections continue to be a very common problem, at least with BPM databases. The condition can manifest itself in different ways. The most common experience of a stale connection is from error messages in the log or FFDCs that contain "StaleConnectionException".
reference:
Based on the provided context, here are the key points regarding the StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases:

1. Stale connections to databases are a common problem, especially with BPM (Business Process Management) databases. This issue persists despite the availability of much published documentation about stale connections.

2. The StaleConnectionException can manifest in different ways, but the most common symptom is the presence of such error messages in the application logs or FFDCs (First Failure Data Capture).

3. The root cause of the StaleConnectionException is often related to the database connection management within the BPM application. When a database connection becomes stale or unusable, the application tries to use it, leading to the StaleConnectionException.

4. Possible reasons for the stale connections include:
   - Inactivity timeout on the database side causing the connection to become stale
   - Issues with the BPM application's connection pooling or connection management logic
   - Conflicts between the BPM application and other applications/services accessing the same database

5. To resolve the StaleConnectionException issue, the following steps can be taken:
   - Ensure that the BPM application is using the latest version of the database driver and that it is compatible with the database version.
   - Review the BPM application's database connection pool settings and tune them as needed to prevent connections from becoming stale.
   - Implement connection validation and connection refresh mechanisms within the BPM application to proactively check and renew database connections.
   - Coordinate with the database team to ensure that the database's connection timeout settings are appropriate for the BPM application's needs.
   - Analyze the application logs and FFDCs to identify any patterns or specific scenarios that may be leading to the StaleConnectionException.

6. Continuous monitoring, troubleshooting, and fine-tuning of the BPM application's database connection management are often required to effectively address the StaleConnectionException issues.

In summary, the StaleConnectionException is a common problem with BPM databases, and a multi-faceted approach involving the BPM application, database, and connection management is often necessary to resolve it.

question: Why is OCR is putting multiple lines on one line? I am running an APT application, and multiple detail lines are getting put on a single line within my .TXT file.  Is there something I can do about this?
reference:
The issue of multiple lines getting put on a single line within your .TXT file when running an APT application might be caused by the way the OCR processing is interpreting the text. It could be related to how the OCR software is handling variations in font types, sizes, or vertical offsets in the text. 

One possible solution to address this issue is to set a parameter that determines the percentage of vertical offset between words that should be considered as separate lines. By adjusting this parameter, you can control how the OCR software determines where to separate lines in the text. Lower values are more likely to split words into separate lines, while higher values are more likely to merge words into a single line. 

Before running the OCR process, you may want to add an action to adjust this parameter in order to improve the recognition results. By setting the appropriate percentage threshold for vertical offset, you may be able to prevent multiple lines from being merged into a single line during the OCR processing. 

Additionally, it's important to ensure that the OCR software is correctly configured to handle the specific formatting and layout of the text in your documents. Check for any settings or options related to text layout recognition that could be impacting how lines are being interpreted during the OCR process. 

If the issue persists, you may need to further investigate the OCR settings and consult the OCR software's documentation for additional guidance on how to handle text layout variations that are causing multiple lines to be combined into one line in your .TXT file.

question: Why is OCR is putting multiple lines on one line? I am running an APT application, and multiple detail lines are getting put on a single line within my .TXT file.  Is there something I can do about this?
reference:
The issue of multiple lines getting put on a single line within your .TXT file when running an APT application might be caused by the way the OCR processing is interpreting the text. It could be related to how the OCR software is handling variations in font types, sizes, or vertical offsets in the text. 

One possible solution to address this issue is to set a parameter that determines the percentage of vertical offset between words that should be considered as separate lines. By adjusting this parameter, you can control how the OCR software determines where to separate lines in the text. Lower values are more likely to split words into separate lines, while higher values are more likely to merge words into a single line. 

Before running the OCR process, you may want to add an action to adjust this parameter in order to improve the recognition results. By setting the appropriate percentage threshold for vertical offset, you may be able to prevent multiple lines from being merged into a single line during the OCR processing. 

Additionally, it's important to ensure that the OCR software is correctly configured to handle the specific formatting and layout of the text in your documents. Check for any settings or options related to text layout recognition that could be impacting how lines are being interpreted during the OCR process. 

If the issue persists, you may need to further investigate the OCR settings and consult the OCR software's documentation for additional guidance on how to handle text layout variations that are causing multiple lines to be combined into one line in your .TXT file.

IBM Integration Designer could not connect to the DataPower appliance. I am using WDP XI52 with Firmware 7.0.0.7 and IID 7.5.1. When I try to connect WDP from [DataPower Appliances] View in IID, I got a error message as follows : "SSL handshake on the connection to the DataPower appliance "x.x.x.x" was not successful. Contact the DataPower administrator." This situations occurred since WDP Firmware had upgraded from 7.0.0.2 to 7.0.0.5. (Now it was upgraded to 7.0.0.7)
Could you please let me know what I should check to solve this problem? Please note that this WDP works normally and a network is normal. Also, I can connect it by using WebGUI and SSH terminal. And I've checked that IP , XML Management Interface Port, Web Management Service Port and account/password are correct.
reference:
Based on the information provided, it seems that the issue is related to the SSL/TLS configuration between the IBM Integration Designer (IID) and the DataPower appliance. Here are some steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve the problem:

1. **Check the SSL/TLS configuration on the DataPower appliance**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS configuration on the DataPower appliance is up-to-date and secure.
   - Verify that the DataPower appliance is configured to use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and that older versions of SSL/TLS (e.g., SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0) are disabled.
   - Ensure that the DataPower appliance is not vulnerable to the BEAST (Browser Exploit Against SSL/TLS) attack by enabling the appropriate mitigations.

2. **Verify the SSL/TLS configuration in IBM Integration Designer (IID)**:
   - In IID, go to the "DataPower Appliances" view and select the DataPower appliance.
   - Right-click on the appliance and select "Properties".
   - In the "Properties" window, go to the "SSL/TLS" tab and ensure that the settings match the configuration on the DataPower appliance.
   - Try connecting to the DataPower appliance again.

3. **Check the SSL/TLS cipher suites**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS cipher suites configured on the DataPower appliance are compatible with the ones supported by IID.
   - You can check the supported cipher suites in IID by going to "Window" > "Preferences" > "WebSphere DataPower" > "SSL/TLS Cipher Suites".

4. **Verify the SSL/TLS certificates**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS certificates used by the DataPower appliance are valid and trusted by IID.
   - If necessary, import the DataPower appliance's SSL/TLS certificate into the trust store used by IID.

5. **Check the network connectivity**:
   - Ensure that the network connection between IID and the DataPower appliance is stable and that there are no firewall or network-related issues.
   - Try connecting to the DataPower appliance from a different network or device to rule out any local network problems.

6. **Update the firmware and IBM Integration Designer (IID)**:
   - Consider upgrading the DataPower appliance firmware to the latest version, as newer versions may include bug fixes or improvements related to SSL/TLS connectivity.
   - Ensure that you are using the latest version of IBM Integration Designer (IID) that is compatible with the DataPower appliance firmware version.

If the issue persists after trying these steps, you may need to contact IBM Support for further assistance in troubleshooting the SSL/TLS connectivity between the IBM Integration Designer and the DataPower appliance.

Contact the DataPower administrator." This situations occurred since WDP Firmware had upgraded from 7.0.0.2 to 7.0.0.5. (Now it was upgraded to 7.0.0.7)
Could you please let me know what I should check to solve this problem? Please note that this WDP works normally and a network is normal. Also, I can connect it by using WebGUI and SSH terminal. And I've checked that IP , XML Management Interface Port, Web Management Service Port and account/password are correct.

Based on the information provided, it seems that the issue is related to the SSL/TLS configuration between the IBM Integration Designer (IID) and the DataPower appliance. Here are some steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve the problem:

1. **Check the SSL/TLS configuration on the DataPower appliance**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS configuration on the DataPower appliance is up-to-date and secure.
   - Verify that the DataPower appliance is configured to use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and that older versions of SSL/TLS (e.g., SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0) are disabled.
   - Ensure that the DataPower appliance is not vulnerable to the BEAST (Browser Exploit Against SSL/TLS) attack by enabling the appropriate mitigations.

2. **Verify the SSL/TLS configuration in IBM Integration Designer (IID)**:
   - In IID, go to the "DataPower Appliances" view and select the DataPower appliance.
   - Right-click on the appliance and select "Properties".
   - In the "Properties" window, go to the "SSL/TLS" tab and ensure that the settings match the configuration on the DataPower appliance.
   - Try connecting to the DataPower appliance again.

3. **Check the SSL/TLS cipher suites**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS cipher suites configured on the DataPower appliance are compatible with the ones supported by IID.
   - You can check the supported cipher suites in IID by going to "Window" > "Preferences" > "WebSphere DataPower" > "SSL/TLS Cipher Suites".

4. **Verify the SSL/TLS certificates**:
   - Ensure that the SSL/TLS certificates used by the DataPower appliance are valid and trusted by IID.
   - If necessary, import the DataPower appliance's SSL/TLS certificate into the trust store used by IID.

5. **Check the network connectivity**:
   - Ensure that the network connection between IID and the DataPower appliance is stable and that there are no firewall or network-related issues.
   - Try connecting to the DataPower appliance from a different network or device to rule out any local network problems.

6. **Update the firmware and IBM Integration Designer (IID)**:
   - Consider upgrading the DataPower appliance firmware to the latest version, as newer versions may include bug fixes or improvements related to SSL/TLS connectivity.
   - Ensure that you are using the latest version of IBM Integration Designer (IID) that is compatible with the DataPower appliance firmware version.

If the issue persists after trying these steps, you may need to contact IBM Support for further assistance in troubleshooting the SSL/TLS connectivity between the IBM Integration Designer and the DataPower appliance.

question:
Why does nco_confpack -export fail with the message "Tool in menu but not found"? 

I tried to export OMNIbus configuration using nco_confpack command and I get the following message:

Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: Close

I've also tried using it with -list command and I get the same error.

Why is this happening?
reference:
Based on the context provided, the issue with the "Tool in menu but not found" error when using the nco_confpack command is due to a mismatch between the configured menu structure and the available tools in the Omnibus environment.

The key points are:

1. The error message indicates that the menu "AlertsMenu" has a tool called "Close" configured, but the tool is not found.

2. This typically happens when the tool configuration in the Omnibus environment has been modified, but the menu structure has not been updated accordingly.

3. When nco_confpack tries to export or list the configuration, it encounters the menu item that references a tool that no longer exists, causing the "Tool in menu but not found" error.

The resolution to this issue is to:

1. Identify the menu and tool configuration that is causing the issue (in this case, the "AlertsMenu" and the "Close" tool).
2. Either:
   - Recreate the "Close" tool in the Omnibus environment and associate it with the "AlertsMenu" menu.
   - Remove the reference to the "Close" tool from the "AlertsMenu" menu configuration.
3. After making the necessary changes, try running the nco_confpack command again.

The key is to ensure that the menu structure and the available tools are in sync, so that nco_confpack can successfully export or list the Omnibus configuration without encountering missing tool references.

java.lang.Exception: java.lang.Exception:com.lombardisoftware.client.delegate.BusinessDelegateException:PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [update LSW_SNAPSHOT set CREATED_ON =?,NAME = ?,ACRONYM = ?,DESCRIPTION = ?,SEQ_NUM = ?,ERROR_COUNTER =?,ORIG_CREATED_ON = ?,ACTIVATED_ON = ?,STATUS = ?,ARCHIVED_ON =?,LAST_MODIFIED = ?,REPOSITORY_BRANCH_ID = ?,CREATED_BY_USER_ID =?,BRANCH_ID = ?,PROJECT_ID = ?,LAST_MODIFIED_BY_USER_ID = ?,CHANGE_DATA= ?,IS_ACTIVE = ?,IS_BLA_ACTIVE = ?,IS_STARTED = ?,IS_INSTALLED =?,IS_BLA_INSTALLED = ?,IS_TIP_DEPLOYED = ?,IS_DEFAULT =?,TIP_DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS = ?,IS_ARCHIVED = ? where SNAPSHOT_ID = ?]; Error for batch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505, SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69; nested exception iscom.ibm.db2.jcc.am.SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException: Error forbatch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505,SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69
How can I deploy my application?
reference:
You are getting the error SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException when deploying a process application because the acronym generation code in BPM 7501 did not take into consideration the acronym of archived snapshots. This resulted in non-unique acronym generation and subsequent Constraint Violations exceptions in the database.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy your application, you need to apply a fix for BPM 7501. You can download the fix package from Fix Central by searching for JR44672. Follow the instructions provided in the fix readme file for installation and apply the fix to your BPM environment. Once the fix is applied, the acronym generation will check for all existing acronyms in archived or unarchived state while generating a unique acronym, thereby preventing the Constraint Violation exceptions during deployment.

reference:
You are getting the error SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException when deploying a process application because the acronym generation code in BPM 7501 did not take into consideration the acronym of archived snapshots. This resulted in non-unique acronym generation and subsequent Constraint Violations exceptions in the database.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy your application, you need to apply a fix for BPM 7501. You can download the fix package from Fix Central by searching for JR44672. Follow the instructions provided in the fix readme file for installation and apply the fix to your BPM environment. Once the fix is applied, the acronym generation will check for all existing acronyms in archived or unarchived state while generating a unique acronym, thereby preventing the Constraint Violation exceptions during deployment.

When I try to deploy an application on a cluster, why is it throwing an ADMA8019E error in the admin console? The application is being deployed at the cluster scope, but my namespace bindings are defined at the cell scope. The error I'm seeing in the admin console is:

ADMA8019E: The resources that are assigned to the application are beyond the deployment target scope. Resources are within the deployment target scope if they are defined at the cell, node, server, or application level when the deployment target is a server, or at the cell, cluster, or application level when the deployment target is a cluster. Assign resources that are within the deployment target scope of the application or confirm that these resources assignments are correct as specified.

I don't see any actual issue with how the JNDI lookup is occurring once the application is deployed. Should I be concerned about this error?
reference:
Based on the information provided, the issue you are facing is related to the scope of the resources defined for your application deployment.

The error ADMA8019E indicates that the resources assigned to the application are beyond the deployment target scope. In other words, the resources required by the application are defined at a higher scope (cell level) than the deployment target (cluster level).

The key points to understand here are:

1. Deployment Target Scope:
   - When deploying to a cluster, the deployment target scope should be at the cell, cluster, or application level.
   - When deploying to a server, the deployment target scope should be at the cell, node, server, or application level.

2. Resource Scope:
   - Resources (e.g., JNDI bindings) need to be defined within the same scope or a higher scope than the deployment target.
   - In your case, the namespace bindings are defined at the cell scope, which is higher than the cluster-level deployment target.

The fact that you don't see any issues with the JNDI lookup at runtime suggests that the application is able to access the required resources. However, the ADMA8019E error indicates a potential deployment-time issue that should be addressed.

To resolve this issue, you have the following options:

1. Modify the resource scope to match the deployment target scope:
   - Redefine the namespace bindings at the cluster scope, so they are within the deployment target scope.
   - This ensures that the resources are properly assigned to the application during deployment.

2. Change the deployment target to the cell scope:
   - Instead of deploying the application at the cluster scope, deploy it at the cell scope.
   - This will make the cell-level resources within the deployment target scope.

While the application may work without addressing this error, it's generally recommended to resolve the ADMA8019E error to ensure a clean and consistent deployment process. The error indicates a potential mismatch between the resource scope and the deployment target scope, which could lead to issues in more complex deployments or future maintenance.

question:
When I try to deploy an application on a cluster, why is it throwing an ADMA8019E error in the admin console? The application is being deployed at the cluster scope, but my namespace bindings are defined at the cell scope. The error I'm seeing in the admin console is:

ADMA8019E: The resources that are assigned to the application are beyond the deployment target scope. Resources are within the deployment target scope if they are defined at the cell, node, server, or application level when the deployment target is a server, or at the cell, cluster, or application level when the deployment target is a cluster. Assign resources that are within the deployment target scope of the application or confirm that these resources assignments are correct as specified.

I don't see any actual issue with how the JNDI lookup is occurring once the application is deployed. Should I be concerned about this error?
reference:
Based on the information provided, the issue you are facing is related to the scope of the resources defined for your application deployment.

The error ADMA8019E indicates that the resources assigned to the application are beyond the deployment target scope. In other words, the resources required by the application are defined at a higher scope (cell level) than the deployment target (cluster level).

The key points to understand here are:

1. Deployment Target Scope:
   - When deploying to a cluster, the deployment target scope should be at the cell, cluster, or application level.
   - When deploying to a server, the deployment target scope should be at the cell, node, server, or application level.

2. Resource Scope:
   - Resources (e.g., JNDI bindings) need to be defined within the same scope or a higher scope than the deployment target.
   - In your case, the namespace bindings are defined at the cell scope, which is higher than the cluster-level deployment target.

The fact that you don't see any issues with the JNDI lookup at runtime suggests that the application is able to access the required resources. However, the ADMA8019E error indicates a potential deployment-time issue that should be addressed.

To resolve this issue, you have the following options:

1. Modify the resource scope to match the deployment target scope:
   - Redefine the namespace bindings at the cluster scope, so they are within the deployment target scope.
   - This ensures that the resources are properly assigned to the application during deployment.

2. Change the deployment target to the cell scope:
   - Instead of deploying the application at the cluster scope, deploy it at the cell scope.
   - This will make the cell-level resources within the deployment target scope.

While the application may work without addressing this error, it's generally recommended to resolve the ADMA8019E error to ensure a clean and consistent deployment process. The error indicates a potential mismatch between the resource scope and the deployment target scope, which could lead to issues in more complex deployments or future maintenance.

The key features included in the "Tools and Utilities" license for IBM Rational Rhapsody are:

- ReporterPro
- Reporter
- RPGetConnected
- RPGraphPanel
- RPRG (Gateway)
- RPXMI (Import/Export XMI)

So the Reporter and ReporterPro features can be used with the Floating license of IBM Rational Rhapsody Architect Software.

reference:
The error message "certificate expired" suggests that the DataPower appliance is still using the old/expired certificate for validation instead of the new one you added. Here are some possible reasons why the new certificate might not be used even after adding it:

1. The new certificate was not properly loaded into the keystore: Double-check that the new certificate was correctly loaded into the appropriate keystore and that the keystore configuration has been updated to use the new certificate for validation.

2. Keystore reference: Ensure that the validation credential configuration in DataPower is correctly referencing the updated keystore that contains the new certificate. Sometimes, the appliance may still be configured to use the old keystore, leading to the validation failure.

3. Cache issue: DataPower might be caching the old certificate information. Try restarting the DataPower appliance to clear any cached references to the old certificate and force it to use the new one.

4. Insufficient permissions: Verify that the user running the DataPower appliance has the necessary permissions to read and use the new keystore and certificates. Insufficient permissions could prevent the appliance from accessing the new certificate data.

5. Configuration error: Review the DataPower configuration settings to ensure that all changes related to the new certificate are correctly made. It's possible that there could be a misconfiguration that is causing the appliance to continue using the expired certificate.

By addressing these potential issues and ensuring that the new certificate is correctly loaded, referenced, and accessible by the DataPower appliance, you should be able to resolve the "certificate expired" error.

Why do I still get "certificate expired" error after adding new certificate? 

The remote SSL vendor has provided us a new certificate to replace an expiring one. We have added the new certificate to the appropriate Datapower validation credential, however, connections are still failing with "certificate expired":

mpgw(Inbound_MPG): tid(51005)[request][10.20xx.xx] gtid(51345): certificate validation failed for '/C=US/O=People Services/OU=IT/CN=test.site.com' against 'My_ValCred': certificate has expired
reference:
The error message "certificate expired" suggests that the DataPower appliance is still using the old/expired certificate for validation instead of the new one you added. Here are some possible reasons why the new certificate might not be used even after adding it:

1. The new certificate was not properly loaded into the keystore: Double-check that the new certificate was correctly loaded into the appropriate keystore and that the keystore configuration has been updated to use the new certificate for validation.

2. Keystore reference: Ensure that the validation credential configuration in DataPower is correctly referencing the updated keystore that contains the new certificate. Sometimes, the appliance may still be configured to use the old keystore, leading to the validation failure.

3. Cache issue: DataPower might be caching the old certificate information. Try restarting the DataPower appliance to clear any cached references to the old certificate and force it to use the new one.

4. Insufficient permissions: Verify that the user running the DataPower appliance has the necessary permissions to read and use the new keystore and certificates. Insufficient permissions could prevent the appliance from accessing the new certificate data.

5. Configuration error: Review the DataPower configuration settings to ensure that all changes related to the new certificate are correctly made. It's possible that there could be a misconfiguration that is causing the appliance to continue using the expired certificate.

By addressing these potential issues and ensuring that the new certificate is correctly loaded, referenced, and accessible by the DataPower appliance, you should be able to resolve the "certificate expired" error.

Here are some steps you can take to troubleshoot and resolve this issue:

1. **Check for Conflicting Processes**: Ensure that no other process is currently using the port 6,002. You can use a tool like "netstat" to check which processes are using this port.

2. **Check WebSphere Application Server Port Configurations**:
   - Verify the port range settings in the WebSphere Application Server V9.0 configuration. Ensure that the starting port number (7000) and the ending port number (8000) do not overlap with any other running applications or services on the system.
   - If the port range is conflicting with other applications, try changing the port range to a different set of available ports.

3. **Disable Firewall or Check Firewall Settings**: Ensure that the firewall is not blocking access to the port 6,002 or the configured port range. You can try temporarily disabling the firewall to see if that resolves the issue.

4. **Check for Any Existing WebSphere Application Server Instances**:
   - Ensure that there are no other instances of WebSphere Application Server V8.4 or V9.0 running on the system. If there are any, stop them and then try starting the V9.0 Launcher again.
   - If you have multiple WebSphere Application Server instances on the same system, make sure they are using different port ranges to avoid conflicts.

5. **Clear Cached Information**:
   - Try clearing any cached information or temporary files related to the WebSphere Application Server V9.0 installation.
   - On Windows, you can try deleting the contents of the "%TEMP%" directory and the "%USERPROFILE%\.was" directory.

6. **Reinstall or Repair WebSphere Application Server V9.0**:
   - As a last resort, you can try reinstalling or repairing the WebSphere Application Server V9.0 installation to ensure that all the necessary components are properly configured.

question:
What things are important to consider when installing a fix pack for IIB running on a multi-instance environment? I am planning to apply a fix pack to my current version of IBM Integration Bus (IIB) using multi-instance brokers and I am looking for any important information regarding the process.

For example:

 

- installation and verification tasks
 

- is it possible to back out this fix pack in case there are issues
 

- any specific tasks for multi instance configuration
reference:
Based on the provided context, here are some important things to consider when installing a fix pack for IIB running on a multi-instance environment:

1. Installation and Verification Tasks:
   - Ensure you have sufficient free disk space on all the systems hosting the IIB instances.
   - Perform a full backup of your current IIB environment, including configurations, databases, and message stores.
   - Apply the fix pack to each IIB instance one by one, following the recommended installation steps.
   - After installing the fix pack on each instance, verify that the instances are running correctly and that there are no issues with message flows, adapters, and other components.
   - Test your critical business applications and flows to ensure they are working as expected.

2. Backout Capability:
   - IIB generally provides the ability to back out a fix pack if needed. Refer to the IIB documentation for the specific steps to revert to the previous version.
   - Before applying the fix pack, ensure you understand the backout process and have the necessary information to perform it, such as the previous fix pack level and any necessary rollback steps.

3. Considerations for Multi-Instance Configuration:
   - Coordinate the fix pack installation across all the IIB instances in your environment to minimize downtime.
   - Ensure the fix pack is applied consistently across all instances. It is recommended to apply the fix pack to one instance at a time and verify its functionality before moving on to the next instance.
   - If your multi-instance environment is configured for high availability or failover, plan the fix pack installation to minimize the impact on your production workloads.
   - Update any scripts or automation used to manage your multi-instance environment to reflect the new fix pack level.
   - Communicate the fix pack installation plan and timeline to your team and stakeholders to set appropriate expectations.

4. Additional Recommendations:
   - Review the fix pack documentation and release notes for any specific instructions or considerations for your IIB version and environment.
   - Consult the IIB support documentation or reach out to IBM Support if you have any questions or encounter issues during the fix pack installation.
   - Consider performing the fix pack installation and testing in a non-production environment first before applying it to your production systems.

By following these guidelines, you can help ensure a smooth and successful fix pack installation for your IIB multi-instance environment, minimize downtime, and have a plan in place to back out the fix pack if needed.

What things are important to consider when installing a fix pack for IIB running on a multi-instance environment? I am planning to apply a fix pack to my current version of IBM Integration Bus (IIB) using multi-instance brokers and I am looking for any important information regarding the process.

For example:

 

- installation and verification tasks
 

- is it possible to back out this fix pack in case there are issues
 

- any specific tasks for multi instance configuration
reference:
Based on the provided context, here are some important things to consider when installing a fix pack for IIB running on a multi-instance environment:

1. Installation and Verification Tasks:
   - Ensure you have sufficient free disk space on all the systems hosting the IIB instances.
   - Perform a full backup of your current IIB environment, including configurations, databases, and message stores.
   - Apply the fix pack to each IIB instance one by one, following the recommended installation steps.
   - After installing the fix pack on each instance, verify that the instances are running correctly and that there are no issues with message flows, adapters, and other components.
   - Test your critical business applications and flows to ensure they are working as expected.

2. Backout Capability:
   - IIB generally provides the ability to back out a fix pack if needed. Refer to the IIB documentation for the specific steps to revert to the previous version.
   - Before applying the fix pack, ensure you understand the backout process and have the necessary information to perform it, such as the previous fix pack level and any necessary rollback steps.

3. Considerations for Multi-Instance Configuration:
   - Coordinate the fix pack installation across all the IIB instances in your environment to minimize downtime.
   - Ensure the fix pack is applied consistently across all instances. It is recommended to apply the fix pack to one instance at a time and verify its functionality before moving on to the next instance.
   - If your multi-instance environment is configured for high availability or failover, plan the fix pack installation to minimize the impact on your production workloads.
   - Update any scripts or automation used to manage your multi-instance environment to reflect the new fix pack level.
   - Communicate the fix pack installation plan and timeline to your team and stakeholders to set appropriate expectations.

4. Additional Recommendations:
   - Review the fix pack documentation and release notes for any specific instructions or considerations for your IIB version and environment.
   - Consult the IIB support documentation or reach out to IBM Support if you have any questions or encounter issues during the fix pack installation.
   - Consider performing the fix pack installation and testing in a non-production environment first before applying it to your production systems.

By following these guidelines, you can help ensure a smooth and successful fix pack installation for your IIB multi-instance environment, minimize downtime, and have a plan in place to back out the fix pack if needed.

question: Launching IBM Rational Software Architect application results in Error: Java was started but returned exit code = -1 At times when you launch Rational Software Architect (RSA) application, you might encounter the following error: Error: Java was started but returned exit code = -1
reference: This error may indicate a problem with the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) when launching IBM Rational Software Architect. To resolve this issue, you can try updating the video driver to the newest version, as outdated or incompatible drivers can cause JVM termination errors. Another possible cause could be related to a bug in the Intel Graphic Card driver for Windows XP Service Pack 3. If updating the video driver does not solve the problem, you should contact Rational support for further assistance.

question: Does the BPM internal Document Store work with IBM DB2 pureScale? I use IBM DB2 pureScale with my BPM installation. During startup of the server and initialization of the internal document store I see hanging threads in the systemOut.log and the process will not finish. How can this be solved?
reference:
Yes, the BPM internal Document Store can work with IBM DB2 pureScale. If you are experiencing hanging threads during startup of the server and initialization of the internal document store, it may be due to issues with the pureScale setup and configuration. 

One potential solution is to ensure that the DB2 JCC properties for DB2 pureScale affinity are correctly configured on Tomcat. This involves setting pureScale member host names in the operating system's hosts file, adding JNDI resource information to the web application environment file, adding JNDI data source information to the Tomcat configuration file, and implementing custom code to retrieve supported user attributes from the underlying security repository.

By correctly configuring the DB2 JCC properties for DB2 pureScale affinity on Tomcat, you may be able to resolve the hanging threads issue during BPM server startup and internal document store initialization.

question: Does the BPM internal Document Store work with IBM DB2 pureScale? I use IBM DB2 pureScale with my BPM installation. During startup of the server and initialization of the internal document store I see hanging threads in the systemOut.log and the process will not finish. How can this be solved?
reference:
Yes, the BPM internal Document Store can work with IBM DB2 pureScale. If you are experiencing hanging threads during startup of the server and initialization of the internal document store, it may be due to issues with the pureScale setup and configuration. 

One potential solution is to ensure that the DB2 JCC properties for DB2 pureScale affinity are correctly configured on Tomcat. This involves setting pureScale member host names in the operating system's hosts file, adding JNDI resource information to the web application environment file, adding JNDI data source information to the Tomcat configuration file, and implementing custom code to retrieve supported user attributes from the underlying security repository.

By correctly configuring the DB2 JCC properties for DB2 pureScale affinity on Tomcat, you may be able to resolve the hanging threads issue during BPM server startup and internal document store initialization.

question: TEP to TEPS communication issues with different Java versions Recent Java updates have caused connection problems when logging into the TEPS via the TEP client (Browser or Java Web Start). Is there an updated list of known issues?
reference:
Based on the provided context, there are a few key points regarding the issues with the Tivoli Enterprise Portal (TEP) client communicating with the Tivoli Enterprise Portal Server (TEPS) when using different Java versions:

1. Java 8 Support:
   - The Tivoli Enterprise Portal client had issues running with Java 8, including problems with Internet Explorer 11 and Firefox.
   - A fix was included in IBM Tivoli Monitoring 6.3.0 Fix Pack 5 (6.3.0-TIV-ITM-FP0005) to add support for Java 8 in the Tivoli Portal clients.

2. Known Issues with Java 8:
   - Using Java 8 64-bit with Internet Explorer 11 failed with the message "This content cannot be displayed in a frame".
   - Workaround: Use Java 8 32-bit with Internet Explorer 11 or use the WebStart client.
   - Java 8 failed with Firefox, resulting in a blank screen.
   - Workaround: Use Internet Explorer or the WebStart client. This issue was expected to be fixed in Oracle Java 8 u60, targeted for August 2015.

3. Java Security Updates:
   - Recent Java updates have caused connection problems when logging into the portal server via the Tivoli Enterprise Portal browser and WebStart clients.
   - Refer to technote #1672459 for important information regarding the latest Java Support requirements: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21672459

In summary, the key issues and known problems are related to the compatibility of the Tivoli Enterprise Portal client with different Java versions, especially Java 8. The IBM Tivoli Monitoring 6.3.0 Fix Pack 5 provided a resolution for the Java 8 support, but there were still some specific issues with Internet Explorer 11 and Firefox that required workarounds. Additionally, recent Java security updates have also caused connection problems, so it's important to monitor the latest Java support requirements for the Tivoli Enterprise Portal environment.

When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requested a remote connection it was matched for sharing with a connection that was still in the process of being established. The WebSphere MQ Client waited for the connection to complete and due to a small timing window began incorrectly sharing the connection without confirming the connection's suitability. If the connection's suitability had been checked then the connection would have been marked unsuitable due to the Negotiated Channel specifying that Conversation Sharing was disabled (SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1). reference:
Based on the provided context, there are a few key points regarding the issues with the Tivoli Enterprise Portal (TEP) client communicating with the Tivoli Enterprise Portal Server (TEPS) when using different Java versions:

1. Java 8 Support:
   - The Tivoli Enterprise Portal client had issues running with Java 8, including problems with Internet Explorer 11 and Firefox.
   - A fix was included in IBM Tivoli Monitoring 6.3.0 Fix Pack 5 (6.3.0-TIV-ITM-FP0005) to add support for Java 8 in the Tivoli Portal clients.

2. Known Issues with Java 8:
   - Using Java 8 64-bit with Internet Explorer 11 failed with the message "This content cannot be displayed in a frame".
   - Workaround: Use Java 8 32-bit with Internet Explorer 11 or use the WebStart client.
   - Java 8 failed with Firefox, resulting in a blank screen.
   - Workaround: Use Internet Explorer or the WebStart client. This issue was expected to be fixed in Oracle Java 8 u60, targeted for August 2015.

3. Java Security Updates:
   - Recent Java updates have caused connection problems when logging into the portal server via the Tivoli Enterprise Portal browser and WebStart clients.
   - Refer to technote #1672459 for important information regarding the latest Java Support requirements: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21672459

In summary, the key issues and known problems are related to the compatibility of the Tivoli Enterprise Portal client with different Java versions, especially Java 8. The IBM Tivoli Monitoring 6.3.0 Fix Pack 5 provided a resolution for the Java 8 support, but there were still some specific issues with Internet Explorer 11 and Firefox that required workarounds. Additionally, recent Java security updates have also caused connection problems, so it's important to monitor the latest Java support requirements for the Tivoli Enterprise Portal environment.

question: Cognos Analytics - Images not displayed in PDF/Excel, working in HTML I've just completed an upgrade to Cognos Analytics 11.0.3. When running existing reports in HTML, the images are displayed but when I try to run them in PDF/Excel they are not.
reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue you are experiencing with images not being displayed in PDF/Excel but working in HTML after upgrading to Cognos Analytics 11.0.3 may be due to permissions, file path configurations, or SSL settings. 

To troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue, you can try the following steps:

1. Check the permissions of the folder containing the images to ensure they are configured correctly.

2. Verify that the images are located within the directory specified in the report.

3. If the image directory is not found, ensure that the images are placed in the specified location.

4. If SSL is enabled and causing issues with image display in PDF, ensure that the SSL certificate Chain of Trust is imported on the Application Tier.

5. Import the CA certificate and any Intermediate certificates in the chain of trust in the IBM Cognos CA keystore using the ThirdPartyCertificateTool.

By following these steps, you may be able to resolve the issue of images not being displayed in PDF/Excel reports in Cognos Analytics 11.0.3.

Error: "MBEANSTARTER LOADEXTENSIONS FAILED TO LOAD EXTENSION" occurs at portal startup We are using Portal Server 8.5 and when starting the Portal server we see following error:

0000005e MBeanStarter E com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.MBeanStarter loadExtensions failed to load extension: key: ServerExt.applications / value: com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions

How can we resolve this error?
reference:
To resolve the error "MBEANSTARTER LOADEXTENSIONS FAILED TO LOAD EXTENSION" that occurs at portal startup in Portal Server 8.5, you can follow these steps:

1) Open the WebSphere Application Server (WAS) admin console.
2) Navigate to Resources -> Resource environment providers -> WP ScriptingService -> Custom properties.
3) Locate an entry with the name "ServerExt.applications" and the value "com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions".
4) Delete this entry, save the changes, and restart the server.

Alternatively, a code fix for this issue is integrated into the WebSphere Portal & WCM Combined Cumulative Fix 05 for Portal 8.5.0.0. You can download this fix from Fix Central using the link provided.

The problem is that with WID, the JRE contains xerces, during builds the plugins use the xerces plugin to load the xmls. The problem occurs when the is run on the main thread, the classloader does not pick up the xerces plugin rather uses the xerces that comes with the JRE, causing a class case exception that's wrapped in the CoreException. The solution is the create our own classloader that uses the plugin classloading first before loading the classes from the JRE. The code changes are in com.ibm.wbit.comptest.ant. java.lang.Exception: java.lang.Exception:com.lombardisoftware.client.delegate.BusinessDelegateException:PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [update LSW_SNAPSHOT set CREATED_ON =?,NAME = ?,ACRONYM = ?,DESCRIPTION = ?,SEQ_NUM = ?,ERROR_COUNTER =?,ORIG_CREATED_ON = ?,ACTIVATED_ON = ?,STATUS = ?,ARCHIVED_ON =?,LAST_MODIFIED = ?,REPOSITORY_BRANCH_ID = ?,CREATED_BY_USER_ID =?,BRANCH_ID = ?,PROJECT_ID = ?,LAST_MODIFIED_BY_USER_ID = ?,CHANGE_DATA= ?,IS_ACTIVE = ?,IS_BLA_ACTIVE = ?,IS_STARTED = ?,IS_INSTALLED =?,IS_BLA_INSTALLED = ?,IS_TIP_DEPLOYED = ?,IS_DEFAULT =?,TIP_DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS = ?,IS_ARCHIVED = ? where SNAPSHOT_ID = ?]; Error for batch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505, SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69; nested exception iscom.ibm.db2.jcc.am.SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException: Error forbatch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505,SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69

reference:
Based on the information provided, the error `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` is occurring during the deployment of a process application on the IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) Process Server. This error is likely due to a unique constraint violation in the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table.

The specific issue seems to be related to the generation of unique acronyms for snapshots. The error message indicates that the update statement for the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table is failing due to a constraint violation, possibly because the generated acronym for the snapshot already exists in the database.

The problem summary and conclusion from the provided context suggest the following:

1. In earlier versions of BPM (7.5.1), the acronym generation code did not consider the acronyms of archived snapshots, leading to non-unique acronym generation and subsequent constraint violations.

2. A fix (APAR JR44672) was made available for BPM 7.5.0 that addresses this issue by checking for all existing acronyms, including those in the archived state, when generating unique acronyms.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy the process application, you can try the following steps:

1. Check if you are using the latest version of BPM with the necessary fixes applied. The provided context mentions that the issue was fixed in a future release, so you should ensure that you are running the latest version of BPM with all the necessary cumulative fixes.

2. If you are still experiencing the issue, you can try the following:
   - Manually review the snapshots in the system and ensure that there are no duplicate or conflicting acronyms, especially for archived snapshots.
   - If you find any duplicate or conflicting acronyms, you can try manually updating or removing the affected snapshots to resolve the constraint violation issue.
   - Alternatively, you can try deploying the process application to a different, clean Process Server instance to see if the issue is isolated to the current environment.

3. If the issue persists, you may need to involve IBM support to further investigate the problem and potentially provide a more specific fix or workaround for your environment.

By following these steps, you should be able to identify and resolve the root cause of the `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` error, allowing you to successfully deploy the process application on the IBM BPM Process Server.

How can I deploy my application?
reference:
Based on the information provided, the error `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` is occurring during the deployment of a process application on the IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) Process Server. This error is likely due to a unique constraint violation in the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table.

The specific issue seems to be related to the generation of unique acronyms for snapshots. The error message indicates that the update statement for the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table is failing due to a constraint violation, possibly because the generated acronym for the snapshot already exists in the database.

The problem summary and conclusion from the provided context suggest the following:

1. In earlier versions of BPM (7.5.1), the acronym generation code did not consider the acronyms of archived snapshots, leading to non-unique acronym generation and subsequent constraint violations.

2. A fix (APAR JR44672) was made available for BPM 7.5.0 that addresses this issue by checking for all existing acronyms, including those in the archived state, when generating unique acronyms.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy the process application, you can try the following steps:

1. Check if you are using the latest version of BPM with the necessary fixes applied. The provided context mentions that the issue was fixed in a future release, so you should ensure that you are running the latest version of BPM with all the necessary cumulative fixes.

2. If you are still experiencing the issue, you can try the following:
   - Manually review the snapshots in the system and ensure that there are no duplicate or conflicting acronyms, especially for archived snapshots.
   - If you find any duplicate or conflicting acronyms, you can try manually updating or removing the affected snapshots to resolve the constraint violation issue.
   - Alternatively, you can try deploying the process application to a different, clean Process Server instance to see if the issue is isolated to the current environment.

3. If the issue persists, you may need to involve IBM support to further investigate the problem and potentially provide a more specific fix or workaround for your environment.

By following these steps, you should be able to identify and resolve the root cause of the `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` error, allowing you to successfully deploy the process application on the IBM BPM Process Server.

reference:
Based on the information provided, the error `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` is occurring during the deployment of a process application on the IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) Process Server. This error is likely due to a unique constraint violation in the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table.

The specific issue seems to be related to the generation of unique acronyms for snapshots. The error message indicates that the update statement for the `LSW_SNAPSHOT` table is failing due to a constraint violation, possibly because the generated acronym for the snapshot already exists in the database.

The problem summary and conclusion from the provided context suggest the following:

1. In earlier versions of BPM (7.5.1), the acronym generation code did not consider the acronyms of archived snapshots, leading to non-unique acronym generation and subsequent constraint violations.

2. A fix (APAR JR44672) was made available for BPM 7.5.0 that addresses this issue by checking for all existing acronyms, including those in the archived state, when generating unique acronyms.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy the process application, you can try the following steps:

1. Check if you are using the latest version of BPM with the necessary fixes applied. The provided context mentions that the issue was fixed in a future release, so you should ensure that you are running the latest version of BPM with all the necessary cumulative fixes.

2. If you are still experiencing the issue, you can try the following:
   - Manually review the snapshots in the system and ensure that there are no duplicate or conflicting acronyms, especially for archived snapshots.
   - If you find any duplicate or conflicting acronyms, you can try manually updating or removing the affected snapshots to resolve the constraint violation issue.
   - Alternatively, you can try deploying the process application to a different, clean Process Server instance to see if the issue is isolated to the current environment.

3. If the issue persists, you may need to involve IBM support to further investigate the problem and potentially provide a more specific fix or workaround for your environment.

By following these steps, you should be able to identify and resolve the root cause of the `SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException` error, allowing you to successfully deploy the process application on the IBM BPM Process Server.

reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue of App Connect Professional Studio crashing without any error message or warning could be caused by a problem with the heap memory allocation for the Studio application. 

To resolve this issue, you can try increasing the size of the heap memory allocated to the Cast Iron Studio by following these steps:

1. Start the Studio through the command line interface using the following command:
   ```
   CastIronStudio.exe -J-Xmx1024m
   ```
   In this command, "1024" represents the new memory size that will be allocated to the Studio instead of the default value of 512. This numeric value is in MB.
   
2. If increasing the heap memory size does not resolve the issue, you may need to open a service request with IBM Cast Iron Support for further assistance.

You can also try using garbage collection from Studio to free up unused space and check the XML Schema preference settings to ensure that the memory usage is within acceptable limits.

question: I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages. How can I determine what happen to the messages?
reference:
Based on the information provided in the context, it seems the issue is related to a problem with queue checkpointing when using a mixture of persistent and non-persistent messages.

The key points are:

1. If a queue manager ends unexpectedly (e.g. due to a sudden machine reboot) rather than being shut down gracefully, it can result in a damaged queue when the queue manager restarts.

2. This is more likely to happen if the queue is used with a mixture of persistent and non-persistent messages, especially for transmit queues.

3. The typical symptoms are that the queue appears to be empty or the queue is reported as damaged, even though persistent messages should still be present.

To determine what happened to the persistent messages in your case, I would suggest the following:

1. Check the queue manager logs around the time the messages went missing. There may be error messages indicating an issue with the queue checkpoint or recovery.

2. Use the IBM Heap Analyzer tool to analyze any heap dumps or Java core files that may have been generated when the issue occurred. This can help identify any problems in the queue manager's internal handling of the messages.

3. Ensure you are always shutting down the queue manager cleanly using the `endmqm` command. Unexpected shutdowns increase the risk of this type of queue corruption.

4. Consider separating persistent and non-persistent messages onto different queues to avoid the potential mixing issue.

5. Apply the relevant fix pack for your version of WebSphere MQ, as the APAR indicates the issue has been addressed in later release levels.

The key is to investigate the queue manager logs and any diagnostic information collected around the time the messages went missing. This should provide clues as to what happened to the persistent messages you were expecting to receive.

question: I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages. How can I determine what happen to the messages?
reference:
Based on the information provided in the context, it seems the issue is related to a problem with queue checkpointing when using a mixture of persistent and non-persistent messages.

The key points are:

1. If a queue manager ends unexpectedly (e.g. due to a sudden machine reboot) rather than being shut down gracefully, it can result in a damaged queue when the queue manager restarts.

2. This is more likely to happen if the queue is used with a mixture of persistent and non-persistent messages, especially for transmit queues.

3. The typical symptoms are that the queue appears to be empty or the queue is reported as damaged, even though persistent messages should still be present.

To determine what happened to the persistent messages in your case, I would suggest the following:

1. Check the queue manager logs around the time the messages went missing. There may be error messages indicating an issue with the queue checkpoint or recovery.

2. Use the IBM Heap Analyzer tool to analyze any heap dumps or Java core files that may have been generated when the issue occurred. This can help identify any problems in the queue manager's internal handling of the messages.

3. Ensure you are always shutting down the queue manager cleanly using the `endmqm` command. Unexpected shutdowns increase the risk of this type of queue corruption.

4. Consider separating persistent and non-persistent messages onto different queues to avoid the potential mixing issue.

5. Apply the relevant fix pack for your version of WebSphere MQ, as the APAR indicates the issue has been addressed in later release levels.

The key is to investigate the queue manager logs and any diagnostic information collected around the time the messages went missing. This should provide clues as to what happened to the persistent messages you were expecting to receive.

question: Limitations of sylog-TCP log target using DataPower Gateways I am trying to configure a log target using type syslog-TCP. It seems that the payload is getting truncated when I try to record custom logs to it using log-action. Why is this? How can I workaround it.
reference:
Based on the context provided, there are a few key points regarding the limitations of using a syslog-TCP log target on DataPower Gateways:

1. Syslog over TCP has no inherent size limitation, unlike syslog over UDP which has a typical 1024 byte limit per packet.

2. However, the DataPower implementation of syslog-TCP may have an internal limit on the size of log messages that can be sent. This could explain why the log payload is getting truncated.

3. The context mentions that the truncation is occurring when trying to record "custom logs" using the log-action. This suggests that the size of the custom log data being generated exceeds the internal limit of the syslog-TCP implementation on DataPower.

Possible workarounds:

1. Reduce the size/content of the custom log data being generated, keeping it within the limits of the syslog-TCP implementation on DataPower.

2. Use a different log target type instead of syslog-TCP, such as:
   - File type log target - This can handle larger log payloads as it writes directly to a file on the DataPower filesystem.
   - HTTP log target - This can POST the log data to an external HTTP server, avoiding any internal size limits.

3. Upgrade to the latest DataPower firmware/fix pack, as later versions may have increased the internal limits for syslog-TCP log targets.

4. Engage IBM support to further investigate the specific size limitations of the syslog-TCP implementation on your DataPower version, and see if there are any other workarounds or configuration options available.

The key is to understand the specific limitations of the syslog-TCP implementation on your DataPower appliance, and then adjust your logging strategy accordingly to ensure full log data is captured as needed.

question: Limitations of sylog-TCP log target using DataPower Gateways I am trying to configure a log target using type syslog-TCP. It seems that the payload is getting truncated when I try to record custom logs to it using log-action. Why is this? How can I workaround it.
reference:
Based on the context provided, there are a few key points regarding the limitations of using a syslog-TCP log target on DataPower Gateways:

1. Syslog over TCP has no inherent size limitation, unlike syslog over UDP which has a typical 1024 byte limit per packet.

2. However, the DataPower implementation of syslog-TCP may have an internal limit on the size of log messages that can be sent. This could explain why the log payload is getting truncated.

3. The context mentions that the truncation is occurring when trying to record "custom logs" using the log-action. This suggests that the size of the custom log data being generated exceeds the internal limit of the syslog-TCP implementation on DataPower.

Possible workarounds:

1. Reduce the size/content of the custom log data being generated, keeping it within the limits of the syslog-TCP implementation on DataPower.

2. Use a different log target type instead of syslog-TCP, such as:
   - File type log target - This can handle larger log payloads as it writes directly to a file on the DataPower filesystem.
   - HTTP log target - This can POST the log data to an external HTTP server, avoiding any internal size limits.

3. Upgrade to the latest DataPower firmware/fix pack, as later versions may have increased the internal limits for syslog-TCP log targets.

4. Engage IBM support to further investigate the specific size limitations of the syslog-TCP implementation on your DataPower version, and see if there are any other workarounds or configuration options available.

The key is to understand the specific limitations of the syslog-TCP implementation on your DataPower appliance, and then adjust your logging strategy accordingly to ensure full log data is captured as needed.
