This MustGather document explains how to troubleshoot this problem by yourself, how to generate diagnostic data when the problem is happening, how to collect the available data from your system, and how share that data with IBM support. SYMPTOM Your Integration Node (broker) fails to respond to a deployment request that was issued by using either the WMB/IIB Toolkit, the Explorer plugin, or the mqsideploy command. You might see a deployment hang/timeout, or BIP2066E errors in the message log. ENVIRONMENT These instructions are for WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris or Windows systems. Return to the WMB / IIB MustGather index [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21209857] for other problems. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM STEP 1: SELF-GUIDED TROUBLESHOOTING A BIP2066E message indicates that a response was not received from your execution group within the time period specified in the ConfigurationChangeTimeout parameter. The default setting for deployment timeouts is 5 minutes (300 seconds), so increase this value only if the timeout was manually reduced to a lower value.

question: Why am I seeing "CWSXM0100E: Multiple replies have been produced for a single request flow in module" ? We are building a simple mediation module, consisting only of the request flow. The mediation module has one service invoke calling an external service through web service binding. Upon testing the process, we observe see that the service invoke is being called twice. There is no Fan-in or fan -out in the request flow. Below is the error: "Caused by: com.ibm.wsspi.sibx.mediation.flow.MediationRuntimeException: CWSXM1023E: Exception when calling flow action: CWSXM0100E: Multiple replies have been produced for a single request flow in module"
reference: The error "CWSXM0100E: Multiple replies have been produced for a single request flow in module" occurs when a mediation primitive is wired more than once to the next mediation primitive. Even though it may seem like there is only one wire, upon closer inspection, multiple wires exist. In this case, the error is likely caused by mistakenly wiring primitives more than once, resulting in the service invoke being called twice during the testing process. To resolve this issue, you should check the wiring of primitives in your mediation module and ensure that redundant wires are deleted. After that, save the project and redeploy the application to the server. This should prevent multiple invocations of the service invoke and eliminate the error message.

SYMPTOM The following error message can be observed in the SystemOut.log file: CWSXM0100E: Multiple replies have been produced for a single request flow in module <module_name> More than one invocation can occur from a single request. CAUSE This error occurs when a mediation primitive is wired more than once to the next mediation primitive. It might seem to be a single wire. However, upon closer inspection, more than one wire exists. By mistake, primitives might be wired more than once when there is only one wire. Delete any redundant wires. 2. Save the project. 3. Redeploy the application to the server. The error "CWSXM0100E: Multiple replies have been produced for a single request flow in module" occurs when a mediation primitive is wired more than once to the next mediation primitive, even though it may seem like a single wire. This can happen when primitives are wired more than once by mistake, and can be resolved by deleting any redundant wires, saving the project, and redeploying the application to the server.

In your case, since you have a simple mediation module with only one service invoke calling an external service, the issue is likely due to a redundant wire. To resolve this, try deleting any redundant wires in your mediation module, save the project, and redeploy the application to the server. This should resolve the issue and prevent the service invoke from being called twice.

question:
Error #2070 I purchased the SPSS grad pack and put one of the licenses on one computer and another on this one. This computer crashed and I was forced to reformat the hard drive. Subsequently, I lost SPSS in the process.  I am now reinstalling with the single user copy option.

The error it gave me now when I attempted to authorize the program with the original authorization number I received was:

Authorization in progress ... (removed) Authorization failed.: You are not allowed to generate any more new licenses. End Of Transaction. All permitted authorizations for the provided authorization code(s) have been utilized. No additional authorizations are permitted on this code. If you think this is an error, please contact IBM Corp. Customer Service at spssls@us.ibm.com ( http://www-01.ibm.com/software/analytics/spss ) with your product and purchase details. Click "Finish" to exit.
reference:
Based on the information provided, it seems that the issue you are encountering is related to the licensing of your SPSS Grad Pack. Here are the key points:

1. You had previously installed SPSS on two different computers using the same authorization code.
2. One of the computers crashed, and you had to reformat the hard drive, resulting in the loss of SPSS on that machine.
3. Now, when you are trying to reinstall SPSS on the same computer using the single user copy option, you are receiving the error "All permitted authorizations for the provided authorization code(s) have been utilized. No additional authorizations are permitted on this code."

The error message indicates that the authorization code you are using has been exhausted, as it was previously used to activate SPSS on two different computers.

To resolve this issue, you will need to contact IBM SPSS Customer Service at spssls@us.ibm.com. Provide them with your product and purchase details, and explain the situation. They should be able to assist you in obtaining a new authorization code or provide guidance on how to proceed.

It's important to note that the SPSS Grad Pack typically allows for installation on multiple computers, but the number of concurrent activations is limited. When you reinstall on a computer where SPSS was previously installed, the system recognizes that the authorization code has been used before and blocks the activation.

The IBM SPSS Customer Service team should be able to help you resolve this issue and get your SPSS Grad Pack up and running again on the desired computer.

The error it gave me now when I attempted to authorize the program with the original authorization number I received was:

Authorization in progress ... (removed) Authorization failed.: You are not allowed to generate any more new licenses. End Of Transaction. All permitted authorizations for the provided authorization code(s) have been utilized. No additional authorizations are permitted on this code. If you think this is an error, please contact IBM Corp. Customer Service at spssls@us.ibm.com ( http://www-01.ibm.com/software/analytics/spss ) with your product and purchase details. Click "Finish" to exit.
reference:
Based on the information provided, it seems that the issue you are encountering is related to the licensing of your SPSS Grad Pack. Here are the key points:

1. You had previously installed SPSS on two different computers using the same authorization code.
2. One of the computers crashed, and you had to reformat the hard drive, resulting in the loss of SPSS on that machine.
3. Now, when you are trying to reinstall SPSS on the same computer using the single user copy option, you are receiving the error "All permitted authorizations for the provided authorization code(s) have been utilized. No additional authorizations are permitted on this code."

The error message indicates that the authorization code you are using has been exhausted, as it was previously used to activate SPSS on two different computers.

To resolve this issue, you will need to contact IBM SPSS Customer Service at spssls@us.ibm.com. Provide them with your product and purchase details, and explain the situation. They should be able to assist you in obtaining a new authorization code or provide guidance on how to proceed.

It's important to note that the SPSS Grad Pack typically allows for installation on multiple computers, but the number of concurrent activations is limited. When you reinstall on a computer where SPSS was previously installed, the system recognizes that the authorization code has been used before and blocks the activation.

The IBM SPSS Customer Service team should be able to help you resolve this issue and get your SPSS Grad Pack up and running again on the desired computer.

I have purchased IBM SPSS Statistics 24.0 client software and licenses, but I am afraid my version 23.0 licenses will expire before I complete my client migrations to Statistics 24.0. How can I keep my end users up and running throughout the migration? CAUSE License for version N expires before all clients can be upgraded to client software version N+1 ANSWER Starting in IBM SPSS Statistics 22.0 we have added what we colloquially call "N+1 Licensing" for this exact problem. Simply put, your Statistics version "N" will use client licenses for Statistics version "N+1". Imagine the above scenario. You have IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 clients deployed and the license period is coming to an end. Your licenses for Statistics 23.0 will expire long before you complete the upgrade of all clients to Statistics 24.0. The solution is to go ahead and deploy your Statistics 24.0 licenses. Statistics 23.0 (version "N") will use a Statistics 24.0 (version "N+1") license. This is true for Authorized User licensing. CONTENT Problem: In cases where the ITCAM monitoring agent uninstall is not successful, the WebSphere Application Servers that were being monitored will no longer start. This happens when ITCAM for WAS configuration parameters defined in each application server do not get removed when the unconfiguration portion of the uninstall fails. Resolution: There are two possible solutions for this issue. 1. Deploy the System Monitoring for WebSphere Application Server again. Once the shared service is deployed, attempt the uninstall again. 2. Manually remove the WebSphere Application Server configuration that is specific to ITCAM and is causing this issue. question: I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.
reference:
Based on the context provided, it seems you are facing an issue with transferring your SPSS 24 Graduate Pack license to a new computer. Here are the steps you can take to resolve this:

1. Contact your SPSS vendor (Hearne, On the Hub, StudentDiscounts.com, JourneyEd, thinkEDU, or Studica) who sold you the SPSS Graduate Pack. Explain the situation that your previous computer was found to be defective, and you need to transfer the license to a new machine.

2. The vendor should be able to help you with the license transfer process. Typically, they will have a process to deactivate the license on the old computer and reactivate it on the new one.

3. Make sure you have the original activation code that was provided to you when you purchased the SPSS Graduate Pack. This activation code will be needed to complete the license transfer.

4. The vendor may also need some information about your new computer, such as the machine ID, to complete the license transfer. They can guide you through the process.

5. If the vendor is unable to resolve the issue, you can also contact IBM SPSS Technical Support for further assistance with the license transfer. Their contact information should be available on the IBM SPSS website.

The key is to work closely with your SPSS vendor, as they should have the necessary processes and tools to help you transfer the license from the old computer to the new one, especially since you have only used the activation code on one machine so far.

I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.
reference:
Based on the context provided, it seems you are facing an issue with transferring your SPSS 24 Graduate Pack license to a new computer. Here are the steps you can take to resolve this:

1. Contact your SPSS vendor (Hearne, On the Hub, StudentDiscounts.com, JourneyEd, thinkEDU, or Studica) who sold you the SPSS Graduate Pack. Explain the situation that your previous computer was found to be defective, and you need to transfer the license to a new machine.

2. The vendor should be able to help you with the license transfer process. Typically, they will have a process to deactivate the license on the old computer and reactivate it on the new one.

3. Make sure you have the original activation code that was provided to you when you purchased the SPSS Graduate Pack. This activation code will be needed to complete the license transfer.

4. The vendor may also need some information about your new computer, such as the machine ID, to complete the license transfer. They can guide you through the process.

5. If the vendor is unable to resolve the issue, you can also contact IBM SPSS Technical Support for further assistance with the license transfer. Their contact information should be available on the IBM SPSS website.

The key is to work closely with your SPSS vendor, as they should have the necessary processes and tools to help you transfer the license from the old computer to the new one, especially since you have only used the activation code on one machine so far.

reference:

1. Stop the SOA Agent.
2. Right-click on the SOA subnodes in the TEP console and choose "Clear offline entry" to make them invisible.
3. Remove the information of the deleted entries from the KD4.dc.properties file located in <ITM_HOME>/TMAITM6/KD4/config on Windows or <ITM_HOME>/<platform>/d4/KD4/config on Unix. Save the changes.

5. Start the SOA Agent.
6. The deleted SOA subnodes should no longer appear in the TEP console after completing these steps.

question: Java.io.NotSerializableException in WAS We are experiencing the Java.io.NotSerializableException exception. I see this error: WTRN0047E:java.io.NotSerializableException. Anyone experienced this before?
reference:
Based on the context provided, the Java.io.NotSerializableException typically occurs when an object that does not implement the `java.io.Serializable` interface is attempted to be serialized or deserialized. This exception can be encountered in scenarios involving Persistent sessions, PMI, and HTTPSession.

To resolve the `java.io.NotSerializableException`, ensure that all objects placed in the HTTPSession implement the `java.io.Serializable` interface. Additionally, you can use the `SessionInspectServlet` provided by WebSphere Application Server to determine which attribute of the session object references a non-serializable object.

If you are experiencing this exception in WAS, it is recommended to check the objects being stored in the session for serialization compatibility and use the `SessionInspectServlet` to identify the issue further and ensure proper implementation of the `java.io.Serializable` interface for all relevant objects.

Based on the context provided, the Java.io.NotSerializableException typically occurs when an object that does not implement the `java.io.Serializable` interface is attempted to be serialized or deserialized. This exception can be encountered in scenarios involving Persistent sessions, PMI, and HTTPSession.

To resolve the `java.io.NotSerializableException`, ensure that all objects placed in the HTTPSession implement the `java.io.Serializable` interface. Additionally, you can use the `SessionInspectServlet` provided by WebSphere Application Server to determine which attribute of the session object references a non-serializable object.

If you are experiencing this exception in WAS, it is recommended to check the objects being stored in the session for serialization compatibility and use the `SessionInspectServlet` to identify the issue further and ensure proper implementation of the `java.io.Serializable` interface for all relevant objects.

Based on the provided context, the issue you are experiencing is related to the replication of data between the primary and secondary Impact servers. The problem is that when the secondary Impact server is started, the primary server's logging stops.

To resolve this issue, you need to check the APAR (APAR NUMBER IZ81446) related to the problem description. According to the APAR, the issue is caused by the inability of the Impact server cluster to replicate data types with user parameters values in excess of 16,000 characters.

To fix this issue, you need to add a new property to the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file on all Impact servers in the cluster. The property is called "replication.file.size.limit" and its value should be set to a suitable limit (e.g., 8192, 16384, 32768, etc.).

Additionally, ensure that there are no trailing white-space characters on the property, as these can invalidate properties in lower versions of Impact.

After adding the property and restarting the Impact servers, the logging should resume on the primary server, and the secondary server should be able to replicate the data correctly.

Note that this issue is specific to Impact 5.1 and is fixed in Impact 5.1 Fix Pack 0001. If you are using a different version of Impact, you may need to check the release notes for your specific version to see if a similar fix is available.

5. **Check environment variables**: Ensure that your system's environment variables are properly set for RFT 8.2. Check the installation guide for the required environment variables and make sure they are configured correctly.

6. **Try running RFT in safe mode**: Start RFT in safe mode by running the following command:

question: IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. Why is this the case?
reference: The reason the IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during the download action on a document is that if the mime type of the document as shown in system properties in ICN is not text/csv, then Navigator cannot recognize the document properly, resulting in adding the .dat extension during download. The correct mime type for a CSV file should be text/csv.

SYMPTOM A .dat extension is added to the CSV document upon download. CAUSE A CSV document is basically a plain text file. If the mime type of the document as shown in system properties in ICN is not text/csv, then Navigator cannot recognize the document and a .dat extension will be added upon download. The correct mime type for a CSV file is text/csv. question:
Why are some Datatypes corrupt after Impact cluster failover/failback ? 

Running Impact 7.1.0.11. The symptom is whenever Impact does a failover, a couple DataTypes
turn out empty.

I've checked the type files before and after Impact failover and the difference happens in the property

*.SQL.USERPARAMETERS

This property no longer exists for the corrupted datatypes".
reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue of some datatypes becoming corrupt after Impact cluster failover/failback is due to the following reasons:

1. APAR IZ81446: This APAR addresses an issue in Impact versions prior to 6.0 where the .type file of the Secondary Impact Server configuration would be truncated if the USERPARAMETERS property value exceeded 16,000 characters.

2. The resolution for this issue is to add a new property to the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file to increase the file size limit for the .type file. The recommended values for this property are 8192, 16384, 32768, etc.

3. The issue occurs because the USERPARAMETERS property, which includes the property name and definition, can exceed 16,000 characters. When the .type file is replicated across the cluster, the truncation leads to the corruption of the datatype.

4. In your case, running Impact 7.1.0.11, the symptom is that the *.SQL.USERPARAMETERS property no longer exists for the corrupted datatypes after the failover/failback.

To resolve this issue, you need to:

1. Ensure that the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file on all Impact servers in the cluster has the property to increase the file size limit, as mentioned in the APAR resolution.
2. Restart the Impact servers after making this change to ensure that the .type file is correctly replicated across the cluster.
3. Monitor the cluster and check the .type files on both the primary and secondary servers to ensure that the datatypes are not being corrupted during failover/failback operations.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the issue of datatype corruption after Impact cluster failover/failback.

[link below] RESOLVING THE PROBLEM Additional comments associated with APAR IZ81446 release notes: "a new property is added to increase the file size limit: * Add the property to $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file where size limit can be 8192, 16384, 32768, etc.. " The property would have to be added to all ImpactServers in the Cluster and would require a restart to enable - ensuring that the ImpactServer started as Primary had the correct, uncorrupted .type file to be replicated across the Cluster. Also ensure that there are no trailing white-space characters on the property as these invalidate properties in lower versions of Impact. The APAR is not an issue in Impact 6 and 7, but one would still have to include this property with an appropriate value to handle a large character length for the USERPARAMETERS parameter.

reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue of some datatypes becoming corrupt after Impact cluster failover/failback is due to the following reasons:

1. APAR IZ81446: This APAR addresses an issue in Impact versions prior to 6.0 where the .type file of the Secondary Impact Server configuration would be truncated if the USERPARAMETERS property value exceeded 16,000 characters.

2. The resolution for this issue is to add a new property to the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file to increase the file size limit for the .type file. The recommended values for this property are 8192, 16384, 32768, etc.

3. The issue occurs because the USERPARAMETERS property, which includes the property name and definition, can exceed 16,000 characters. When the .type file is replicated across the cluster, the truncation leads to the corruption of the datatype.

4. In your case, running Impact 7.1.0.11, the symptom is that the *.SQL.USERPARAMETERS property no longer exists for the corrupted datatypes after the failover/failback.

To resolve this issue, you need to:

1. Ensure that the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file on all Impact servers in the cluster has the property to increase the file size limit, as mentioned in the APAR resolution.
2. Restart the Impact servers after making this change to ensure that the .type file is correctly replicated across the cluster.
3. Monitor the cluster and check the .type files on both the primary and secondary servers to ensure that the datatypes are not being corrupted during failover/failback operations.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the issue of datatype corruption after Impact cluster failover/failback.

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
reference:
To resolve the issue of the silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent failing due to the "SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement" message, you can follow these steps:

1. Check the MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt file and ensure that the line "License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license." is correctly formatted.

2. Make sure that the complete path to the silent response file (MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt) is specified correctly when launching the silent uninstall command. This is important because if the path is not specified, it can result in the failure of the silent uninstall process.

3. Adjust the command to include the full path to the silent response file when launching the silent uninstall. For example, the command should look like this:
```
start /wait setup /z"/sfE:\TEMP\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

By following these steps, you should be able to successfully perform a silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent without encountering the "You must agree to the License Agreement" error message.

question:
Why are some Datatypes corrupt after Impact cluster failover/failback ? 

Running Impact 7.1.0.11. The symptom is whenever Impact does a failover, a couple DataTypes
turn out empty.

I've checked the type files before and after Impact failover and the difference happens in the property

*.SQL.USERPARAMETERS

This property no longer exists for the corrupted datatypes".
reference: The corrupt datatypes after Impact cluster failover/failback are caused by the property *.SQL.USERPARAMETERS no longer existing for those datatypes. The difference in the type files before and after the failover shows that this property is missing, resulting in the datatypes turning out empty.
contexts: netcool; impact; netcool/impact; nci; data; type; datatype; .type; replication; cluster; sync; error; 500; mark; invalid TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) The DataType is not being correctly replicated across the ImpactServer Cluster SYMPTOM The .type file of the Secondary ImpactServer configuration is truncated with the error message: * * CAUSE APAR "IZ81446: IMPACT 511 CLUSTER UNABLE TO REPLICATE DATATYPES WITH USERPARMETERS VALUES IN EXCESS OF 16,000 CHARACTERS." [link below] RESOLVING THE PROBLEM Additional comments associated with APAR IZ81446 release notes: "a new property is added to increase the file size limit: * Add the property to $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file where size limit can be 8192, 16384, 32768, etc.. " The property would have to be added to all ImpactServers in the Cluster and would require a restart to enable - ensuring that the ImpactServer started as Primary had the correct, uncorrupted .type file to be replicated across the Cluster. Also ensure that there are no trailing white-space characters on the property as these invalidate properties in lower versions of Impact. The APAR is not an issue in Impact 6 and 7, but one would still have to include this property with an appropriate value to handle a large character length for the USERPARAMETERS parameter.

answer:
The problem is caused by the APAR "IZ81446: IMPACT 511 CLUSTER UNABLE TO REPLICATE DATATYPES WITH USERPARMETERS VALUES IN EXCESS OF 16,000 CHARACTERS." The issue is that the property *.SQL.USERPARAMETERS is being truncated, causing the datatypes to become corrupt.

To resolve the issue, you need to add a new property to the $NCHOME/impact/etc/<SERVERNAME>_server.props file, which will increase the file size limit. The property should be added to all ImpactServers in the Cluster and requires a restart to enable. Additionally, ensure that there are no trailing white-space characters on the property, as these can invalidate properties in lower versions of Impact.

question:
How to resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server? I see this exception in WebSphere Application Server J2c and RRA traces:

WSRdbManagedC > preTestConnection Entry WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl@51a507f2 query: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL WSRdbManagedC 3 Exception java.sql.SQLException: ORA-02396: exceeded maximum idle time, please connect again DSRA0010E: SQL State = 61000, Error Code = 2,396 at oracle.jdbc.driver.T4CTTIoer.processError(T4CTTIoer.java:440) at 
...
Entry java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01012: not logged on ..... OracleDataSto < findMappingClass return Exit class com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException
reference:
Based on the provided context, the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server is likely caused by the ORA-02396 error, which indicates that the maximum idle time for the database connection has been exceeded.

To resolve this issue, you can try the following steps:

1. **Increase the database connection timeout**: In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the values for properties like "connectionTimeout" and "loginTimeout" to a higher value, for example, 300 seconds.

2. **Increase the statement cache size**: Increasing the statement cache size can help reuse prepared statements and reduce the frequency of new connections being created. In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the "statementCacheSize" property to a higher value, for example, 100.

3. **Adjust the connection pool settings**: Ensure that the connection pool settings, such as "maximumPoolSize" and "minimumPoolSize", are configured appropriately for your application's load. You may need to increase the maximum pool size to allow more concurrent connections.

4. **Monitor and identify long-running SQL statements**: Use database monitoring tools or review the WebSphere Application Server logs to identify any long-running SQL statements that may be holding onto connections for an extended period, causing the connection pool to be exhausted. Optimize these SQL statements or implement appropriate connection management strategies in your application.

5. **Consider using a connection refresh strategy**: Configure the datasource to periodically check the validity of the connections in the pool and refresh them if necessary. This can be done by setting the "connectionCheckupInterval" property in the WebSphere Application Server administration console.

By implementing these steps, you should be able to resolve the StaleConnectionException and improve the overall performance and stability of your WebSphere Application Server application when interacting with the Oracle database.

answer:
To resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server, you can try the following solutions:

1. **Configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool**:
	* Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout.
	* Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout.
2. **Add "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" to the definition of stored procedure on the host**:
	* This can be done as a workaround, but be aware that it may cause issues with XA transactions.
	* Check the technote 1433093 for restrictions on using this clause.
	* Apply APAR IZ07301 if necessary.
3. **Upgrade the JCC driver**:
	* The fix for this issue is incorporated in JCC driver version 3.59.81, which was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later (defect 134363).
4. **Check the database connection**:
	* Verify that the database connection is still valid and not closed externally by a firewall or the remote database due to inactivity.

By trying these solutions, you should be able to resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server.

Based on the provided context, the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server is likely caused by the ORA-02396 error, which indicates that the maximum idle time for the database connection has been exceeded.

To resolve this issue, you can try the following steps:

1. **Increase the database connection timeout**: In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the values for properties like "connectionTimeout" and "loginTimeout" to a higher value, for example, 300 seconds.

2. **Increase the statement cache size**: Increasing the statement cache size can help reuse prepared statements and reduce the frequency of new connections being created. In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the "statementCacheSize" property to a higher value, for example, 100.

3. **Adjust the connection pool settings**: Ensure that the connection pool settings, such as "maximumPoolSize" and "minimumPoolSize", are configured appropriately for your application's load. You may need to increase the maximum pool size to allow more concurrent connections.

4. **Monitor and identify long-running SQL statements**: Use database monitoring tools or review the WebSphere Application Server logs to identify any long-running SQL statements that may be holding onto connections for an extended period, causing the connection pool to be exhausted. Optimize these SQL statements or implement appropriate connection management strategies in your application.

5. **Consider using a connection refresh strategy**: Configure the datasource to periodically check the validity of the connections in the pool and refresh them if necessary. This can be done by setting the "connectionCheckupInterval" property in the WebSphere Application Server administration console.

By implementing these steps, you should be able to resolve the StaleConnectionException and improve the overall performance and stability of your WebSphere Application Server application when interacting with the Oracle database.

To resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server, you need to configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool. Specifically, you should:

* Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout.
* Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout.

You can find more information on how to configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool in the following document: http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/udat_conpoolset.html

WSRdbManagedC > preTestConnection Entry WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl@51a507f2 query: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL WSRdbManagedC 3 Exception java.sql.SQLException: ORA-02396: exceeded maximum idle time, please connect again DSRA0010E: SQL State = 61000, Error Code = 2,396 at oracle.jdbc.driver.T4CTTIoer.processError(T4CTTIoer.java:440) at

reference:
Based on the provided context, the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server is likely caused by the ORA-02396 error, which indicates that the maximum idle time for the database connection has been exceeded.

To resolve this issue, you can try the following steps:

1. **Increase the database connection timeout**: In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the values for properties like "connectionTimeout" and "loginTimeout" to a higher value, for example, 300 seconds.

2. **Increase the statement cache size**: Increasing the statement cache size can help reuse prepared statements and reduce the frequency of new connections being created. In the WebSphere Application Server administration console, go to "Resources" > "JDBC Providers" > select the provider for your Oracle datasource > "Data sources" > select your datasource > "Custom properties" tab. Increase the "statementCacheSize" property to a higher value, for example, 100.

3. **Adjust the connection pool settings**: Ensure that the connection pool settings, such as "maximumPoolSize" and "minimumPoolSize", are configured appropriately for your application's load. You may need to increase the maximum pool size to allow more concurrent connections.

4. **Monitor and identify long-running SQL statements**: Use database monitoring tools or review the WebSphere Application Server logs to identify any long-running SQL statements that may be holding onto connections for an extended period, causing the connection pool to be exhausted. Optimize these SQL statements or implement appropriate connection management strategies in your application.

5. **Consider using a connection refresh strategy**: Configure the datasource to periodically check the validity of the connections in the pool and refresh them if necessary. This can be done by setting the "connectionCheckupInterval" property in the WebSphere Application Server administration console.

By implementing these steps, you should be able to resolve the StaleConnectionException and improve the overall performance and stability of your WebSphere Application Server application when interacting with the Oracle database.

Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
reference:
The error message "SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement" indicates that the silent uninstall process is still expecting the license agreement to be accepted, even though the response file contains the line "License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license."

Here are the steps to resolve the issue:

1. Ensure that the silent response file (`MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`) is correctly formatted and located in the expected path.

2. Verify that the license agreement acceptance line in the response file is exactly as follows:
   `acceptLicense=true`

   The response file should look something like this:
   ```
   acceptLicense=true
   ...
   ```

3. If the above step doesn't work, try creating a new, empty response file and add only the `acceptLicense=true` line to it.

4. Run the silent uninstall command again, but this time specify the full path to the response file:
   `start /wait setup /z"C:\path\to\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"`

   Make sure to replace `C:\path\to\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` with the actual path to your response file.

The key point is to ensure that the license agreement acceptance is explicitly set to `true` in the response file, and that the full path to the response file is provided in the command.

Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
reference:
The error message "SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement" indicates that the silent uninstall process is still expecting the license agreement to be accepted, even though the response file contains the line "License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license."

Here are the steps to resolve the issue:

1. Ensure that the silent response file (`MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`) is correctly formatted and located in the expected path.

2. Verify that the license agreement acceptance line in the response file is exactly as follows:
   `acceptLicense=true`

   The response file should look something like this:
   ```
   acceptLicense=true
   ...
   ```

3. If the above step doesn't work, try creating a new, empty response file and add only the `acceptLicense=true` line to it.

4. Run the silent uninstall command again, but this time specify the full path to the response file:
   `start /wait setup /z"C:\path\to\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"`

   Make sure to replace `C:\path\to\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` with the actual path to your response file.

The key point is to ensure that the license agreement acceptance is explicitly set to `true` in the response file, and that the full path to the response file is provided in the command.

confpack; objectserver; omnibus; two TECHNOTE (FAQ) QUESTION What causes the error: "Duplicate menu path: MapPageOVMenu" when using nco_confpack to export or import object server data? CAUSE Due to having 2 menus with the same name in the tools menu. ANSWER The solution is to rename or delete away (if no not needed) one of the duplicate menus. The object server is able to allow for duplicate menu item names because it tracks them by a numeric identifier in the database tables. For nco_confpack to be able to export and then import , it can't rely upon those numeric identifiers, because they will be different from one host to another, so we have to use the name. The menus and menu items are tracked by constructing a menu tree, starting from the root. Then the complete path is then used as the key. This allows for the menu and menu items to be unique, based upon a name. This is where the duplicate menu path comes into the picture. Solution : Make sure the names are unique. For example, append them with a sequential number (ie: by appending a 1, 2, 3....).

CAUSE Due to having 2 menus with the same name in the tools menu. ANSWER The solution is to rename or delete away (if no not needed) one of the duplicate menus. For nco_confpack to be able to export and then import , it can't rely upon those numeric identifiers, because they will be different from one host to another, so we have to use the name. The menus and menu items are tracked by constructing a menu tree, starting from the root. Then the complete path is then used as the key. This allows for the menu and menu items to be unique, based upon a name. This is where the duplicate menu path comes into the picture. Solution : Make sure the names are unique. For example, append them with a sequential number (ie: by appending a 1, 2, 3....).

Hide a page in dotedit step  I am working on datacap 8.1 version. I have 2 pages in a batch. Page 1 with status as 1, Page 2 with status as 20. Both are of same page type. In verification step (dotedit) I want to hide the page which is with status 20. I have given status 20 in ignored page status in web administrator for verify. But still when I navigate through pages in dotedit batch view the respective panel is loading. I am able to submit the batch even if I have one page in a batch with 20 as status.

Is there any way to delete the page (we have multiple same type of pages in a batch) from dotedit based on the page status?
reference:
To hide a page in DotEdit based on its status in IBM Datacap Taskmaster Capture 8.1, you can follow these steps:

1. Create a special page type called "DeleteMe" attached at the batch level.
2. Use an action like "BlankPagesIDBySize(1000, DeleteMe)" to identify the page with status 20.
3. Create a rule with the action "DeleteChildType(DeleteMe)" and attach it at the batch level to remove all pages with the page type "DeleteMe".

By following these steps, you can effectively hide the page with status 20 in DotEdit during verification. This will prevent the panel from loading for that specific page and allow you to navigate through and submit the batch with only the desired pages visible.

1. Create a special page type called "DeleteMe" attached at the batch level.
2. Use an action like "BlankPagesIDBySize(1000, DeleteMe)" to identify the page with status 20.
3. Create a rule with the action "DeleteChildType(DeleteMe)" and attach it at the batch level to remove all pages with the page type "DeleteMe".

reference:
Based on the provided context, the NullPointerException issue when bootstrapping the object store or accessing Site Preferences/Access Role on WorkplaceXT is caused by an invalid entry in the User Display Name Attribute or Group Display Name Attribute setting in the Directory Services Configuration in FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM).

The key points are:

1. The NullPointerException is occurring in the PrefAccessRolesInfoPage and PrefBootstrapInfoPage classes, which are trying to resolve user names and groups defined within the Access Roles based on the Directory Service configuration.

2. If the user name query resolves to null or there is an invalid entry, a NullPointerException error may occur.

3. To resolve the problem, you need to go to FEM and change the User Display Name Attribute or Group Display Name Attribute to a valid LDAP entry such as cn, displayName or uid, and then restart the FileNet Content Engine and Workplace XT instances.

In summary, the root cause of the NullPointerException is an invalid Directory Services Configuration, and the resolution is to update the configuration with a valid LDAP entry for the user and group display name attributes.

answer:
This behavior may occur if an invalid entry has been specified in the User Display Name Attribute or Group Display Name Attribute setting in the Directory Services Configuration in FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM). Workplace XT attempts to resolve the user names and groups defined within the Access Roles based on the Directory Service configuration defined in FEM. If the user name query resolves to null or if there is an invalid entry a NullPointerException error may occur. 

In FEM, change the User Display Name Attribute or Group Display Name Attribute to a valid LDAP entry such as cn, displayName or uid and restart the FileNet Content Engine and Workplace XT instances.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM Review the following points in order to prevent this problem from occurring: * Avoid using a health monitor against the EJB/bootstrap port. * The preferred load balancer health monitor for P8 Content Engine is to use the CE start-up context page, also known as the CE ping page. This should be configured against the HTTP port: http://<<server>>:<<port>>/FileNet/Engine * A typical load balancer HTTP health monitor configuration will only require the context path string: /FileNet/Engine * The monitor interval should be set to the largest practical time interval, typically greater than 5 seconds. and a time-out value of not less than 15 seconds. * The Content Engine application server instance will need to be re-started to close the accumulated open connections. question: where is the websphere application server 9.0.0.4 fix for developers I am using the was 9.0.0.0 in rad/rsa 9.6.1 for Windows. reference:
Based on the information provided in the context, there does not appear to be a specific "Developers" edition available for WebSphere Application Server 9.0.0.4. The options mentioned are the standard editions - Base, Network Deployment, DMZ Secure Proxy Server, and IBM Web Enablement for IBM i.

The context indicates that for WebSphere Application Server 8.5.5, a Developers edition was available, but this does not seem to be the case for version 9.0.0.4.

The recommended solution from the information provided is to apply the Interim Fix PI82587 to your WebSphere Application Server 9.0.0.0 installation that you are using with Rational Application Developer (RAD) 9.6.1. This Interim Fix is available for 9.0.0.3 and 9.0.0.4 versions, but there does not appear to be a specific "Developers" edition available.

So in summary, the Developers edition you are looking for does not seem to exist for WebSphere Application Server 9.0.0.4. The options are to apply the Interim Fix PI82587 to your existing 9.0.0.0 installation, or potentially upgrade to 9.0.0.3 or 9.0.0.4 and then apply the Interim Fix.

1. Contact IBM SPSS support for assistance with transferring your license. You can find support contact information on the IBM SPSS website or through the vendor from whom you purchased your license (e.g. Hearne, On the Hub, StudentDiscounts.com, JourneyEd, thinkEDU, Studica).

2. Explain your situation to the support representative, indicating that your previous computer was defective and you are trying to transfer your license to a new computer.

3. Provide the support representative with your activation code and any other relevant information they may require to verify your license.

4. The support representative should be able to assist you in deactivating the license from your old computer and activating it on your new computer.

5. Follow any instructions provided by the support representative to successfully transfer your SPSS 24 license to your new machine.

By following these steps and contacting IBM SPSS support, you should be able to resolve the issue with the error message you are receiving when trying to activate the license on your new computer.

But, in this case, it is not good to simply increase the maximum number of open cursors in the Oracle database. The root cause is that bind variable is not used in your SQL integration service. The SQL string that is passed to the SQL integration service contains literal values. Because most of the SQL statements for one SQL integration service have different literal values, a matching statement cannot be found in statement cache (shared pool). The cache hit ratio is very low and the execution plan is generated for each SQL statement every time. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM To resolve this issue, use a bind variable in your SQL integration service. The key points from the context are:

1. The ORA-01795 error occurs when there are more than 1000 attributes or merchandising associations per catalog entry in the WebSphere Commerce Management Center.

2. The issue was addressed by APAR LI74800 for WebSphere Commerce V6.0 and APAR JR50396 for WebSphere Commerce V7.0.

Given that your issue is with the Decision Center Business Console in ODM 8.7.0.0, and the error message is similar, it's likely that you are hitting a similar issue with the underlying SQL queries exceeding the Oracle 1000 expression limit.

The recommended course of action would be:

1. Check if there is an available fix or APAR for the specific version of ODM you are using (8.7.0.0) that addresses this issue.

2. If no fix is available, you can try the local fix mentioned in the context, which is to run a full preprocess/buildindex rather than a delta index when the number of entries exceeds 1000.

3. Consult with IBM support to see if they can provide a more specific solution for your ODM 8.7.0.0 environment.

The key is to identify and address the root cause of the SQL query exceeding the Oracle expression limit, which seems to be the underlying issue based on the information provided.

question: Is there a scripting feature in ITM? Is there a scripting feature in ITM?
reference: Yes, there is a scripting feature in ITM. The context mentions that in order to generate a report showing the "up time" of managed systems in IBM Tivoli Monitoring environment, one can write a script to execute a query and calculate the up time based on the GBLTMSTAMP value. This indicates that scripting skills are required to achieve certain tasks in ITM.
contexts: - NT for Windows OS agent This is an overview of the scripting feature; details will be provided in the following sections. The OS agent loops, at a configurable interval, looking for script definition property files (*.properties) in a configurable directory path. The property files are parsed and OS Monitoring Agent spawns a new process named “fcp_daemon” if at least one valid script definition is found. This new daemon is responsible for scheduling the script executions and gathering all information regarding running scripts. According to another configurable interval, the OS agent loops getting the execution script results from the fcp_daemon. The OS Agent is able to parse the script standard output, splitting each row in up to 16 attributes. An event is sent for each standard output row of the script and these events can be caught by pure event situations. 1.1 Quick Start ================ The feature is enabled with default values as soon as the OS agent is started. The only action to start using the feature is the following: - create a property file under default directory (on Linux/UNIX is $CANDLEHOME/localconfig/<product code>/scripts_definitions, on Windows is %CANDLE_HOME%\localconfig\nt\scripts_definitions) using as an example the provided template script_property.txt. Only two properties are

In this case script outputs are visible on TEP console workspaces but no situations will be displayed and no historical collection data will be collected. No TEP workspace changes are introduced by this APAR, but a new built-in query named "Script execution results sampled", based on the new sampled tables, is provided. question: IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. Why is this the case?
reference:
Based on the provided context, the reason why IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during the Download action is because the MIME type of the CSV document is not set correctly in the content repository.

The key points are:

1. A CSV document is a plain text file, and the correct MIME type for it should be "text/csv".

2. If the MIME type of the CSV document in the content repository is not "text/csv", then IBM Content Navigator cannot recognize it as a CSV file.

3. As a result, when the user tries to download the CSV document, IBM Content Navigator adds a .dat extension to the file, as it cannot determine the correct file type.

The context indicates that this issue is caused by the incorrect MIME type of the CSV documents in the content repository. To resolve this, the recommendation is to either:

1. Manually change the MIME type of the affected CSV documents in the content repository using the repository's client APIs.
2. Use a workaround to save the downloaded .dat file and then associate it with a text editor like Notepad to open it.

So, in summary, the .dat extension is added due to the incorrect MIME type of the CSV documents, and the resolution involves either fixing the MIME type in the repository or using a workaround to open the downloaded files.

question: IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during Download action on a document. Why is this the case?
reference:
Based on the provided context, the reason why IBM Content Navigator v2.0.3 is adding a .dat extension to a CSV file during the Download action is because the MIME type of the CSV document is not set correctly in the content repository.

The key points are:

1. A CSV document is a plain text file, and the correct MIME type for it should be "text/csv".

2. If the MIME type of the CSV document in the content repository is not "text/csv", then IBM Content Navigator cannot recognize it as a CSV file.

3. As a result, when the user tries to download the CSV document, IBM Content Navigator adds a .dat extension to the file, as it cannot determine the correct file type.

The context indicates that this issue is caused by the incorrect MIME type of the CSV documents in the content repository. To resolve this, the recommendation is to either:

1. Manually change the MIME type of the affected CSV documents in the content repository using the repository's client APIs.
2. Use a workaround to save the downloaded .dat file and then associate it with a text editor like Notepad to open it.

So, in summary, the .dat extension is added due to the incorrect MIME type of the CSV documents, and the resolution involves either fixing the MIME type in the repository or using a workaround to open the downloaded files.

SYMPTOM Your Integration Node (broker) fails to respond to a deployment request that was issued by using either the WMB/IIB Toolkit, the Explorer plugin, or the mqsideploy command. ENVIRONMENT These instructions are for WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris or Windows systems. question: When should I use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers? MQ version 7.0 introduced a new feature, conversation sharing. Are there any special values on DataPower when configuring conversation sharing?
reference:
Based on the provided context, here are the key points regarding when to use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers:

1. Conversation sharing in WebSphere MQ (WMQ) was introduced in version 7.0 and later. It allows multiple conversations to share a single TCP/IP channel instance.

2. In DataPower, the MQ queue manager (mq-qm) object has a "Sharing Conversations" attribute that can be configured. This setting needs to be coordinated with the SHARECNV attribute on the WMQ SVRCONN channel.

3. There are three main use cases for configuring conversation sharing in DataPower:

   a. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 0, set "Sharing Conversations" to 0 or 1 in DataPower to disable sharing regardless of the WMQ SVRCONN setting.

   b. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1, set "Sharing Conversations" to 1 in DataPower and also enable "Share Single Conversation". This allows each TCP/IP channel instance to have a single conversation.

   c. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more, set "Sharing Conversations" to 2 or more in DataPower to match the WMQ SVRCONN channel setting.

4. For older DataPower firmware versions (7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x), it's recommended to use the case #1 approach with a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. Newer firmware versions (7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later) can use cases #2 and #3.

5. Enabling conversation sharing can provide performance benefits, especially when processing mixed message sizes, as it allows leveraging WMQ V7+ features like read-ahead and buffer management. But it needs to be configured carefully to avoid stability issues.

In summary, the key is to align the "Sharing Conversations" setting in the DataPower mq-qm object with the SHARECNV attribute on the WMQ SVRCONN channel, following the guidance provided for the different use cases based on the negotiated sharing conversations value.

This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. As part of this process the list of known TCP/IP connections are matched for their suitability, this list includes connections which are in the process of being established (MQCONN reply not received from the Queue Manager). question: When should I use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers? MQ version 7.0 introduced a new feature, conversation sharing. Are there any special values on DataPower when configuring conversation sharing?
reference:
Based on the provided context, here are the key points regarding when to use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers:

1. Conversation sharing in WebSphere MQ (WMQ) was introduced in version 7.0 and later. It allows multiple conversations to share a single TCP/IP channel instance.

2. In DataPower, the MQ queue manager (mq-qm) object has a "Sharing Conversations" attribute that can be configured. This setting needs to be coordinated with the SHARECNV attribute on the WMQ SVRCONN channel.

3. There are three main use cases for configuring conversation sharing in DataPower:

   a. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 0, set "Sharing Conversations" to 0 or 1 in DataPower to disable sharing regardless of the WMQ SVRCONN setting.

   b. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1, set "Sharing Conversations" to 1 in DataPower and also enable "Share Single Conversation". This allows each TCP/IP channel instance to have a single conversation.

   c. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more, set "Sharing Conversations" to 2 or more in DataPower to match the WMQ SVRCONN channel setting.

4. For older DataPower firmware versions (7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x), it's recommended to use the case #1 approach with a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. Newer firmware versions (7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later) can use cases #2 and #3.

5. Enabling conversation sharing can provide performance benefits, especially when processing mixed message sizes, as it allows leveraging WMQ V7+ features like read-ahead and buffer management. But it needs to be configured carefully to avoid stability issues.

In summary, the key is to align the "Sharing Conversations" setting in the DataPower mq-qm object with the SHARECNV attribute on the WMQ SVRCONN channel, following the guidance provided for the different use cases based on the negotiated sharing conversations value.

question: Why is MQ pattern showing installed MQ version as 8.0.0.2, instead of 8.0.0.4 when client tries to deploy pattern at the MQ 8.0.0.4 version in PureApplication System? In the pattern, it was clearly showing MQ version 8.0.0.4. After deployment, client checked the MQ version on the Virtual Machine and it shows 8.0.0.2 instead.
reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue seems to be related to a problem in the IBM Pure Application System when trying to install or migrate to IBM MQ 8.0.0.4. The key points are:

1. The IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier have an issue where they can only install IBM MQ 8.0.0.2, even though the pattern-type may have a later version of IBM MQ (e.g., 8.0.0.4).

2. This is due to an interface change in IBM Pure Application System 2.1.2.0 and later versions, which prevents the installation and upgrade of IBM MQ to the latest maintenance level contained in the pattern-type.

3. The symptom is that the installation appears to succeed, but IBM MQ 8.0.0.2 is installed, and the subsequent fixpack update to 8.0.0.4 is not applied.

The resolution provided in the technote is to use a new maintenance.py lifecycle script, which can be obtained from IBM Fix Central. This script enables the installation and migration of the latest maintenance level of IBM MQ contained in the pattern-type, even on the affected IBM Pure Application System releases.

In summary, the mismatch between the expected IBM MQ version (8.0.0.4) and the actual installed version (8.0.0.2) is due to a known issue in the IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier, which has been addressed by IBM with the new maintenance.py script.

question: Why is MQ pattern showing installed MQ version as 8.0.0.2, instead of 8.0.0.4 when client tries to deploy pattern at the MQ 8.0.0.4 version in PureApplication System? In the pattern, it was clearly showing MQ version 8.0.0.4. After deployment, client checked the MQ version on the Virtual Machine and it shows 8.0.0.2 instead.
reference:
Based on the provided context, the issue seems to be related to a problem in the IBM Pure Application System when trying to install or migrate to IBM MQ 8.0.0.4. The key points are:

1. The IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier have an issue where they can only install IBM MQ 8.0.0.2, even though the pattern-type may have a later version of IBM MQ (e.g., 8.0.0.4).

2. This is due to an interface change in IBM Pure Application System 2.1.2.0 and later versions, which prevents the installation and upgrade of IBM MQ to the latest maintenance level contained in the pattern-type.

3. The symptom is that the installation appears to succeed, but IBM MQ 8.0.0.2 is installed, and the subsequent fixpack update to 8.0.0.4 is not applied.

The resolution provided in the technote is to use a new maintenance.py lifecycle script, which can be obtained from IBM Fix Central. This script enables the installation and migration of the latest maintenance level of IBM MQ contained in the pattern-type, even on the affected IBM Pure Application System releases.

In summary, the mismatch between the expected IBM MQ version (8.0.0.4) and the actual installed version (8.0.0.2) is due to a known issue in the IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier, which has been addressed by IBM with the new maintenance.py script.

The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack. 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record. SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below. SYMPTOM Refer to CVE-2011-3389 RESOLVING THE PROBLEM The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance. The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack. 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record. DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2. DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.

question: What process do i neet to follow to upgrade our SPSS Modeler deployment (concurrent license) from v16 to v18? We have 5 users with SPSS Modeler 16 installed using the Concurrent license manager supplied for that version. We need to upgrade to v18.  Do we need to upgrade the license manager as well?
reference:
Based on the provided information, to upgrade your SPSS Modeler deployment from version 16 to version 18 with a concurrent license, you would need to follow these steps:

1. Upgrade the SPSS Modeler software on all client machines from version 16 to version 18.

2. You will also need to upgrade the SPSS Concurrent License Manager from the version that was supplied for Modeler 16 to the version that is compatible with Modeler 18.

The SPSS Concurrent License Manager is a separate component that manages and distributes the concurrent licenses for SPSS products like Modeler. When you upgrade the SPSS Modeler software, you typically need to upgrade the License Manager as well to ensure compatibility and proper license management.

The key steps would be:

- Obtain the required Modeler 18 software and licenses from IBM.
- Upgrade the Modeler software on all client machines from v16 to v18.
- Upgrade the SPSS Concurrent License Manager to the version that supports Modeler 18.
- Configure the new License Manager to work with your 5 concurrent user licenses.
- Test the upgraded Modeler 18 deployment to ensure all users can access it properly using the concurrent licenses.

IBM provides documentation and support resources to help with the license manager upgrade process. The support links provided in the context indicate you may be able to find step-by-step guidance there as well.

question: What process do i neet to follow to upgrade our SPSS Modeler deployment (concurrent license) from v16 to v18? We have 5 users with SPSS Modeler 16 installed using the Concurrent license manager supplied for that version. We need to upgrade to v18.  Do we need to upgrade the license manager as well?
reference:
Based on the provided information, to upgrade your SPSS Modeler deployment from version 16 to version 18 with a concurrent license, you would need to follow these steps:

1. Upgrade the SPSS Modeler software on all client machines from version 16 to version 18.

2. You will also need to upgrade the SPSS Concurrent License Manager from the version that was supplied for Modeler 16 to the version that is compatible with Modeler 18.

The SPSS Concurrent License Manager is a separate component that manages and distributes the concurrent licenses for SPSS products like Modeler. When you upgrade the SPSS Modeler software, you typically need to upgrade the License Manager as well to ensure compatibility and proper license management.

The key steps would be:

- Obtain the required Modeler 18 software and licenses from IBM.
- Upgrade the Modeler software on all client machines from v16 to v18.
- Upgrade the SPSS Concurrent License Manager to the version that supports Modeler 18.
- Configure the new License Manager to work with your 5 concurrent user licenses.
- Test the upgraded Modeler 18 deployment to ensure all users can access it properly using the concurrent licenses.

IBM provides documentation and support resources to help with the license manager upgrade process. The support links provided in the context indicate you may be able to find step-by-step guidance there as well.

question: Why is MQ pattern showing installed MQ version as 8.0.0.2, instead of 8.0.0.4 when client tries to deploy pattern at the MQ 8.0.0.4 version in PureApplication System? In the pattern, it was clearly showing MQ version 8.0.0.4. After deployment, client checked the MQ version on the Virtual Machine and it shows 8.0.0.2 instead.
reference: The issue occurred because of an interface change in IBM Pure Application System 2.1.2.0 and later. Even though the client tried to deploy the pattern at MQ version 8.0.0.4, due to this change, the installation and upgrade of IBM MQ at the latest maintenance level contained in the pattern-type failed. The installation appeared to succeed, but IBM MQ 8.0.0.2 was installed instead and the subsequent fixpack update was not applied. This restriction affected IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier, preventing the installation of versions later than 8.0.0.2.

For example: The following files are created on UNIX / Windows if $TEMP is /tmp:

/tmp/.com_ibm_tools_attach/_notifier
reference:
Based on the provided context, the files created in the $TEMP directory upon IBM Integration Bus (IIB) or WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) startup are:

1. Files in the `/tmp/.com_ibm_tools_attach` directory, such as:
   - `_attachlock`
   - `_master`
   - `_notifier`

These files have unnecessary execute permissions and only owner, group, and world read and write permissions are required.

The problem is that the Java VM was creating these files with unnecessarily broad permissions, creating security concerns. It was also not handling the case where certain files had incorrect permissions.

The temporary fix provided is to run the following command to correct the permissions:

```
chmod 666 /tmp/.com_ibm_tools_attach/_*
```

This should be done without changing permissions on the directories themselves, as doing so could delay VM shutdown.

The permanent fix for this issue was included in the following releases:

- 6.0.1 SR2
- 7.0.0 SR1
- 6.0.0 SR11

The changes included:
- The default permissions for the attach API common files have been changed.
- The recovery algorithm was fixed to handle files with insufficient permissions.

So in summary, the 0 byte files created in the $TEMP/.com_ibm_tools_attach directory are related to the attach API used by IIB/WMB, and the issue with unnecessary permissions on these files has been resolved in the later service releases.

SYMPTOM CIWEB Error: com.ibm.ecm.beans.viewer.DocServicesSessionBean$ICNStreamingDocServices. _loadDocument java.io.IOException: No such file or directory CAUSE ICN creates a subdirectory under UNIX: /tmp or Windows:\temp for temporary file storage. On some systems, automated housecleaning procedures at OS level delete the contents of /tmp and its subdirectories, resulting in the error. DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM On startup, ICN sets the variable ENGINE_TEMPDIR which defines a temporary directory, for example: '/tmp/ECMClient.IBMWebSphereApplicationServer80.navigator.tmpdir' . Verify the directory path and check whether the directory exists or has been deleted. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM There are two ways to resolve the problem: 1) Disable the automation which deletes the contents of /tmp. Some Linux systems for example use a 'tmpwatch' process which deletes files in /tmp. For tmpwatch, an 'EXCLUDE' job parameter can be defined, causing the process to skip the named subdirectory. 2) ICN uses the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) default temp file directory, which can be overridden at JVM level by adding the Java system property java.io.tmpdir. For example, specify "-Djava.io.tmpdir=/var/temp" in the application server startup configuration. Note that this setting is JVM-wide and will affect all applications

question:
Additional steps to apply fix pack to Decision Center 

We are upgrading ODM 8.8.1 Decision Center to the latest 8.8.1.3.

Are there any additional steps to apply the fixpack to Decision Center after we install the fixpack with Installation Manager?
reference:
Based on the information provided, here are the additional steps to apply the fix pack to Decision Center after installing the fix pack using IBM Installation Manager:

1. Repackage your client applications with the up-to-date libraries.
2. Reapply any product customizations to the up-to-date Java EE modules (EARs and WARs).
   - Note that all customizations you developed before the update, such as modifications of the descriptors, must be reapplied to the new, up-to-date EARs and WARs.
   - It's recommended to document and automate these customizations using scripts to make the process easier and error-proof.
3. Update the Decision Center application in your application server:
   - Update the jrules-teamserver-<server>.ear application.
   - Make sure you do not change the class loading policies for applications and modules (parent last for all ODM modules).

So in summary, the key additional steps are to repackage client applications, reapply any customizations, and update the Decision Center application in the application server after installing the fix pack.

question:
Additional steps to apply fix pack to Decision Center 

We are upgrading ODM 8.8.1 Decision Center to the latest 8.8.1.3.

Are there any additional steps to apply the fixpack to Decision Center after we install the fixpack with Installation Manager?
reference:
Based on the information provided, here are the additional steps to apply the fix pack to Decision Center after installing the fix pack using IBM Installation Manager:

1. Repackage your client applications with the up-to-date libraries.
2. Reapply any product customizations to the up-to-date Java EE modules (EARs and WARs).
   - Note that all customizations you developed before the update, such as modifications of the descriptors, must be reapplied to the new, up-to-date EARs and WARs.
   - It's recommended to document and automate these customizations using scripts to make the process easier and error-proof.
3. Update the Decision Center application in your application server:
   - Update the jrules-teamserver-<server>.ear application.
   - Make sure you do not change the class loading policies for applications and modules (parent last for all ODM modules).

So in summary, the key additional steps are to repackage client applications, reapply any customizations, and update the Decision Center application in the application server after installing the fix pack.
